Airbnb revenue rises 17% in second quarter as bookings accelerate
Airbnb said second-quarter revenue advanced 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion, with growth of 13% on an ex-FX basis, as demand lifted bookings across its regions.
The company reported gross booking value of $27.2 billion, up 16%, while nights and seats booked climbed 10% to 148.3 million. Its average daily rate was $184, up 5% from a year earlier, and its implied take rate was 13.2%.
Net income was $816 million, for a net income margin of 23%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 21% to $1.3 billion, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 35%.
The company said app bookings remained a driver, with nights booked on its app increasing 23% and accounting for 64% of total nights booked. First-time bookers grew 11%, and bedroom nights booked rose over 12%.
Free cash flow was $1.3 billion, up 30%, with a 35% margin, while trailing twelve month free cash flow reached $4.8 billion at a 37% margin. The company repurchased $1.1 billion of Class A common stock during the quarter and held $12.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and restricted cash as of June 30, 2026.
For the third quarter, the company expects revenue of $4.69 billion to $4.77 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 15% to 17%. For full-year 2026, it now expects revenue growth to improve to at least mid teens and a full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5%.

[s2] Q2 2026 Shareholder Letter Over the first half of 2026, we’ve delivered some of our strongest results in years.
[s3] In Q2, that momentum accelerated as we exceeded our outlook across every key metric.
[s4] Revenue grew 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion.
[s5] GBV grew 16% year-over-year to $27.2 billion, driven by continued strong demand as well as a moderate increase in Average Daily Rate (“ADR”).
[s6] Nights and Seats Booked grew 10% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1 2026.
[s7] Net income was $816 million and Adjusted EBITDA increased 21% year-over- year to $1.3 billion, representing an expansion in Adjusted EBITDA Margin to 35%.
[s8] One of the most encouraging trends in Q2 was that we saw year-over-year growth accelerate not just in our expansion markets, but in many of our largest core markets as well.
[s9] In fact, net origin nights booked in the U.S., France, the UK, and Australia all accelerated in Q2, reinforcing our confidence that our product innovation is driving demand across our business.
[s10] On key initiatives, we’ve reduced the time from concept to delivery by as much as 60%.
[s11] And compared to the same period last year, we’ve increased the number of features and improvements we’ve shipped this year by nearly 80%.
[s12] Our 2026 Summer Release marked the next step in that journey. ¦ Airbnb Services: We expanded Airbnb Services to include grocery delivery, car rentals, airport pickups, and luggage storage.
[s13] It’s still early days, but we’re seeing real momentum—both in guests’ bookings and how quickly we’re scaling these partner services. ¦ Airbnb Experiences: We added thousands of new Experiences across our most in-demand categories, increasing Airbnb Experiences supply by nearly 80% year-over-year in Q2 2026.
[s14] As our selection grew, demand grew alongside it, with seats booked accelerating year-over- year and quarter-over-quarter. ¦ Boutique and independent hotels: We added thousands of boutique and independent hotels to Airbnb across more than 20 top destinations, including New York, Paris, London, Madrid, Rome, and Singapore, with more markets coming this year.
[s15] Featured hotels come with a price 1 match guarantee and up to 15% Airbnb credit that guests can use toward their next booking.

[s18] Our AI assistant, now available in more than 50 languages, has 3 been rated the best AI support assistant in travel.
[s19] Nearly 45% of issues that begin with our AI assistant are now resolved without a human agent, up from Q1, while delivering much faster resolution times.

[s29] In Q2, our customer support related cost per booking declined approximately 16% year-over-year, driven in part by improvements to our AI assistant.
[s30] The FIFA World Cup 2026™ is one recent example of this strategy in action.
[s31] More than 150,000 homes across host cities were listed on Airbnb for the first time, helping provide an economic uplift for the local community.
[s32] Outlook We’re pleased with the results we’ve delivered in the first half of 2026, and are excited about the continued traction from our product innovation and strong demand on our platform across all regions that is driving momentum in the second half of 2026.
[s33] Q3 2026 ¦ We expect to generate revenue of $4.69 billion to $4.77 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 15% to 17%, inclusive of an approximate three percentage point FX tailwind after factoring in our hedging program.
[s34] We expect our implied take rate to remain relatively in-line year-over-year. ¦ We expect year-over-year GBV growth to be in the mid teens, driven by low double-digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked and a moderate increase in ADR due to mix shift and price appreciation. ¦ We expect Adjusted EBITDA to increase year-over-year and Adjusted EBITDA Margin to be down slightly compared to Q3 2025, due to timing of investments.
[s35] Full-year 2026 ¦ For full-year 2026, we now expect year-over-year revenue growth to improve to at least mid teens, supported by the accelerated pace of Nights and Seats Booked we’ve observed, traction from product and growth initiatives, as well as continued strong travel demand. ¦ For 2026, we now expect to deliver a full-year Adjusted EBITDA Margin of at least 35.5%— an improvement from 2025 that reflects stronger topline growth and underlying operating leverage in our core business, while continuing to invest behind opportunities to drive future growth.
[s36] Business and Financial Performance Q2 2026 148.3M $27.2B Nights and Seats Booked Gross Booking Value 10% Y/Y 16% Y/Y 15% Y/Y (ex-FX) In Q2 2026, Nights and Seats Booked grew 10% year-over-year, representing an acceleration relative to Q1 2026, primarily driven by strong demand across all regions and continued momentum behind our product roadmap including search and merchandising, pricing and tools, and flexible payments.
[s37] Additionally, growth continued to be driven in part by our app strategy, with nights booked on our app in Q2 2026 increasing 23% year-over-year and accounting for 64% of total nights booked—up from 59% in the prior-year period.
[s38] In addition, we saw year-over-year growth of first-time bookers accelerate to 11% in Q2 2026—the highest in four years—with continued strong growth in Brazil, Japan, and India.
[s39] In Q2 2026, GBV was $27.2 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of 16%.
[s40] On an ex-FX basis, GBV increased 15% year-over-year—two percentage points higher than Q1 2026—driven by improving growth of Nights and Seats Booked, as well as an increase in ADR.
[s41] ADR was $184 in Q2 2026, increasing 5% compared to Q2 2025.
[s42] On an ex-FX basis, ADR in Q2 2026 increased 4% year-over-year and was up across all regions— particularly North America and EMEA—due to price appreciation and mix.
[s43] Specifically, in Q2 2026, we saw entire homes, especially listings with four or more bedrooms continue to grow the fastest.
[s44] Bookings on a bedroom basis clearly show this preference for togetherness: while Nights and Seats Booked grew 10% year-over-year in Q2 2026, Bedroom Nights Booked—nights booked multiplied by bedroom count— grew over 12%, continuing a multi-year pattern.
[s45] In fact, over the trailing twelve months through Q2 2026, guests booked more than 1 billion bedroom nights on Airbnb—the highest on record.
[s46] In Q2, we leaned into local marketing campaigns in key growth markets, reinforcing relevancy to each country.
[s47] ¦ North America: In North America, we saw high-single digit growth of Nights and Seats Booked during Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025—representing the highest growth we’ve seen in almost three years.
[s48] ADR in North America increased 7% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, driven by both price appreciation and mix shift.
[s49] Growth in short-term stays and entire homes, particularly listings with four or more bedrooms, continued to outpace long-term stays (trips of 28 days or more) and private rooms, extending a mix-shift trend we have now seen for over a year. ¦ EMEA: In EMEA, we saw high-single digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked during Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, accelerating from Q1 2026.
[s50] ADR in EMEA increased 7% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025.
[s51] On an ex-FX basis, ADR increased 5% compared to Q2 2025, primarily driven by price appreciation. ¦ Latin America: In Latin America, we saw approximately 20% growth in Nights and Seats Booked during Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025.
[s52] ADR in Latin America increased 9% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, primarily driven by FX.
[s53] On an ex-FX basis, ADR increased 2% compared to Q2 2025.
[s54] Brazil continued to see meaningful demand, with origin net nights booked accelerating to over 30% year-over-year growth and the number of first-time bookers increasing 40% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025.
[s55] Overall, we continue to observe market share gains broadly across Latin America, demonstrating the success of our expansion strategy within this region. ¦ Asia Pacific: In Asia Pacific, we saw high-teens growth in Nights and Seats Booked during Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025.
[s56] ADR in Asia Pacific increased 1% in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025.
[s57] Our hyper-local approach to Asia Pacific is yielding positive results in countries like Japan, where in Q2 2026, origin net nights booked grew in the high-teens year-over-year, driven by continued momentum for domestic travel.
[s58] Additionally, we saw origin net nights booked in India accelerate to 60% year-over-year, and the number of first-time bookers in Q2 2026 more than doubled compared to Q2 2025.
[s59] For example, in preparing for the World Cup, in October 2025 we began targeting prospective hosts across 16 cities and added over 150,000 listings by first time hosts for the event.

AEP Q3 2026: Earnings Beat Prior Year, Investment Plan Expanded
Third-quarter profitability climbed on both a GAAP and operating basis, while demand commitments underpinned a larger long-term capital programme.

American Electric Power reported third-quarter 2026 GAAP earnings of $1,187 million, or $2.18 per share, up from $972 million, or $1.82 per share, in third-quarter 2025. Operating earnings rose to $1,216 million, or $2.23 per share, compared with $963 million, or $1.80 per share, a year earlier, extending the strong year-to-date performance cited by the company.

The centrepiece alongside the results was an expanded $100 billion five-year capital plan through 2031, intended to strengthen reliability, modernise the grid and support growing customer demand. The plan is expected to lift rate base to $162 billion by 2031, supported by a 13% plus rate base compound annual growth rate. Within the programme, approximately $37 billion is planned for transmission assets and $36 billion for generation resources, the latter backed by long-term customer contracts.

Demand visibility also increased during the quarter. With 15 gigawatts of new load commitments signed in the third quarter, incremental contracted load is expected to grow to 84 GW by 2031. Large load contracts in integrated states are now expected to generate up to $21 billion in fixed cost offsets for existing residential customers over the life of the contracts.

Outlook: AEP expects full-year 2026 operating earnings to be at or above the high end of its guidance range of $6.25 to $6.55 per share. The company introduced operating earnings guidance of $6.75 to $7.05 per share for 2027 and $7.40 to $7.70 per share for 2028, and introduced an expected annual operating earnings per share growth rate of 9% to 11% from 2027 through 2031.

[s8] COLUMBUS, Ohio, October 28, 2026 - American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) today reported third-quarter 2026 GAAP earnings of $1,187 million or $2.18 per share, compared with GAAP earnings of $972 million or $1.82 per share in third-quarter 2025.
[s9] Operating earnings for third-quarter 2026 were $1,216 million or $2.23 per share, compared with operating earnings of $963 million or $1.80 per share in third-quarter 2025.
[s10] AEP expects full-year results to be at or above the high end of its 2026 operating earnings guidance range of $6.25 to $6.55 per share.
[s11] AEP is also announcing an expanded $100 billion five-year capital plan through 2031 and a new long-term operating earnings growth outlook as accelerating electricity demand creates significant investment opportunities across the company’s service territory.
[s12] The updated capital plan is expected to support a robust 13% plus rate base compound annual growth rate (CAGR) through 2031.
[s13] AEP is further introducing an expected annual operating earnings per share growth rate of 9% to 11% from 2027 through 2031, with a greater than 10% CAGR through 2031 based off the original 2026 guidance midpoint of $6.30 per share.
[s14] The company is also issuing operating earnings guidance ranges of $6.75 to $7.05 per share and $7.40 to $7.70 per share for 2027 and 2028, respectively.
[s15] integrated states are now expected to generate up to $21 billion in fixed cost offsets, increased from $16 billion, for existing residential customers over the life of the contracts.
[s16] With 15 gigawatts (GW) of new load commitments signed during the third quarter, AEP’s incremental contracted load is expected to grow to 84 GW by 2031.
[s17] AEP’s expanded five-year capital plan of $100 billion includes significant investment needs to strengthen reliability, modernize the grid and support growing customer demand.
[s18] As a result, AEP’s rate base is expected to grow to $162 billion by 2031.
[s19] Building on its position as the nation’s largest owner and operator of transmission, the company plans to invest approximately $37 billion in transmission assets as part of the new capital plan.
[s20] Accordingly, AEP’s transmission rate base is expected to nearly double and approach $70 billion by 2031.
[s21] AEP also plans to invest $36 billion in generation resources across its portfolio through 2031 to meet the increased demand, which is backed by long-term customer contracts.
[s22] Approximately $22 billion of capital is planned for distribution, with investments focused on increasing the reliability and resiliency of the grid.

[s24] Given the strong year-to-date performance, AEP expects full-year 2026 operating earnings to be at or above the high end of the guidance range of $6.25-$6.55 per share and introduced operating earnings guidance ranges of $6.75 to $7.05 per share for 2027 and $7.40 to $7.70 per share for 2028.

# American Tower Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

American Tower reported third-quarter results shaped by non-cash revenue comparisons and unrealized investment losses, while raising parts of its full-year outlook and continuing share repurchases.

**Profitability**
- Results were pressured by a decrease in non-cash straight-line revenue, which represented approximately **$(24.0) million** in the current period, compared with approximately **$27.7 million** in the prior-year period.
- Unrealized losses on equity investments were approximately **$(71.5) million**, compared with unrealized gains of approximately **$10.9 million** in the prior-year period.

**Segment Performance and Outlook**
- Citing Data Centers segment outperformance, the company raised the midpoint of its full-year outlook for property revenue by **$55 million**.
- The midpoint for net income was lowered by **$30 million**, primarily due to unrealized losses for equity securities.
- The midpoint for AFFO attributable to common stockholders per share was raised by **$0.02**, primarily due to capital allocation decisions.
- Full-year property revenue midpoint growth rates included **(3.0)%** for U.S. & Canada, **11.0%** for Latin America, **16.2%** for Africa & APAC, **10.4%** for Europe and **16.1%** for Data Centers.

**Capital Expenditures and Balance Sheet**
- Total capital expenditures climbed to approximately **$407 million**, including **$48 million** for non-discretionary capital improvements and corporate capital expenditures.
- The Net Leverage Ratio was **4.9x** net debt to annualized Adjusted EBITDA.
- Total liquidity stood at approximately **$10.6 billion**, consisting of approximately **$1.9 billion** in cash and cash equivalents plus approximately **$8.7 billion** available under revolving credit facilities.

**Capital Returns**
- The company repurchased approximately **1.8 million** shares for an aggregate of approximately **$315 million**.
- Approximately **$1.1 billion** remained available under the stock repurchase program before an authorization to purchase up to an additional **$2.0 billion** of outstanding common stock.

**Bottom Line**
The company faced notable non-cash and investment-related headwinds, but Data Centers strength supported a higher property revenue outlook, while liquidity remained substantial and capital returns continued.

American Water Works Q3 2026: Adjusted EPS Advances as Guidance Narrows
Adjusted earnings climbed in the third quarter, supported by regulated rate recovery despite weather headwinds and higher costs to fund investment.

Third-quarter adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings rose to $2.00 per share from $1.89 per share a year earlier, while GAAP earnings were steady at $1.94 per share. For the year-to-date period, adjusted earnings increased to $4.63 per share from $4.40 per share. Operating revenues grew by $60 million in the quarter and $212 million over the nine-month period, helped by new rates recovering capital and acquisition investments, though unfavorable weather weighed on the quarterly comparison.

The Regulated Businesses drove profitability, with net income climbing to $407 million in the third quarter from $383 million a year earlier. Over the first nine months, segment net income jumped to $946 million from $872 million. Regulatory execution remained a central support, with $284 million of additional annualized revenues authorized since the start of the year, while pending rate cases and infrastructure surcharges seek a further $360 million on an annualized basis.

Capital deployment stayed elevated as the company invested $2.8 billion in infrastructure improvements and growth during the first nine months, including $437 million for regulated acquisitions. The full-year investment plan of $3.7 billion remains on track. Shareholders will receive a quarterly cash dividend of $0.8950 per share, underlining continued capital returns alongside the heavy spending program.

Outlook: Management narrowed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.07 to $6.12 and initiated standalone 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.53 to $6.63, reflecting growth of 8% at the midpoint versus the 2026 range. Long-term targets were affirmed, including EPS growth of 7-9%, providing a clear framework for regulated investment and earnings progression.

# Best Buy Q2 FY2027 Earnings Summary

Best Buy delivered stronger second-quarter results, highlighted by comparable sales growth of **4.1%**, as diluted EPS jumped **70%** to **$1.48**.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Domestic revenue climbed **4.3%** to **$9.07 billion**, driven by comparable sales growth of **4.5%**.
- Domestic online revenue grew **5.1%** on a comparable basis to **$3.00 billion**.
- International revenue slipped **4.2%** to **$709 million**, reflecting a comparable sales decline of **1.8%** and foreign exchange pressure.

**Profitability**
- Adjusted diluted EPS rose **15%** to **$1.47**.
- The domestic gross profit rate expanded to **24.0%**, up from **23.4%** last year.
- Domestic adjusted SG&A was **$1.78 billion**.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- The company returned **$239 million** to shareholders in the quarter.
- That total included dividends of **$203 million** and share repurchases of **$36 million**.

**Outlook**
- The company raised its FY27 revenue guidance to **$42.3 billion** to **$42.8 billion**.
- Comparable sales are now expected to rise **1.9%** to **3.0%** for FY27.
- Adjusted diluted EPS guidance was lifted to **$6.70** to **$6.90**.

**Bottom Line**
The company combined solid domestic growth and improved profitability with increased full-year guidance, signaling confidence heading into the second half.

Baker Hughes Q3 2026: Strong Orders and Record IET Backlog
Record Industrial & Energy Technology backlog and solid adjusted profitability defined a quarter led by order momentum.

Revenue reached $8,025 million, climbing 19% sequentially and 14% year-over-year, while GAAP diluted EPS was $0.41 and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.70. Attributable net income came to $411 million, while adjusted net income was $695 million. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1,415 million, rising 15% sequentially.

Orders were $10.8 billion, lifting remaining performance obligations to $46.4 billion, including record IET RPO of $39.4 billion. Oilfield Services & Equipment orders were $4,047 million, with revenue of $3,660 million and Segment EBITDA of $659 million. Industrial & Energy Technology orders hit $5,886 million, revenue was $3,477 million, and Segment EBITDA was $685 million. Chart contributed revenue of $888 million and Segment EBITDA of $156 million following its acquisition during the quarter.

Cash generation remained healthy, with cash flows from operating activities of $1,005 million and free cash flow of $769 million, supporting the balance of growth investment and capital discipline.

Outlook: Broad-based demand across data centers, space, LNG and gas infrastructure, together with ongoing capacity expansions, supports raising the full-year IET order guidance and Horizon 2 IET order outlook to $50 billion plus.

Caterpillar Q2 2026: First Quarter Above $20 Billion in Sales
Caterpillar delivered record quarterly sales as growth across its main equipment segments lifted revenue and profitability sharply.

Sales and revenues rose to $20.5 billion, up 24% from $16.6 billion a year earlier. Operating profit climbed to $4.295 billion, up 50%, with operating profit margin expanding to 20.9% from 17.3% and adjusted operating profit margin reaching 21.9%. Profit per share increased to $7.77 from $4.62, while adjusted profit per share came in at $8.17.

Power & Energy sales grew to $8.238 billion, up 17%, and segment profit rose to $2.027 billion. Construction Industries was the fastest-growing major segment, with sales surging to $8.346 billion, up 35%, and segment profit advancing to $1.947 billion. Resource Industries sales climbed to $4.648 billion, up 20%, while segment profit increased to $693 million.

Financial Products revenues rose to $1.145 billion. Enterprise operating cash flow was $4.4 billion, and the company ended the quarter with $6.7 billion of enterprise cash. Capital returns included $1.5 billion deployed for repurchases of Caterpillar common stock and $0.7 billion for dividends.

Outlook: With no quantified guidance provided in the release, investors will watch for updates on sales volume and price realization, manufacturing costs, tariff recoveries, restructuring tied to divestitures, and credit conditions at Cat Financial.

Chubb Q3 2026: Underwriting and Investment Income Drive Core Earnings
Core profitability remained strong in the third quarter, supported by excellent P&C underwriting and record adjusted investment income despite modest premium growth.

Chubb reported net income of $2.84 billion, or $7.30 per share, alongside core operating income of $2.98 billion, or $7.66 per share. Consolidated net premiums written climbed to $15.1 billion, up 1.9%, as P&C premiums rose 1.9% and Life Insurance premiums grew 1.4%.

P&C underwriting income reached $2.1 billion, producing a combined ratio of 84.1%, while the current accident year combined ratio excluding catastrophe losses stood at 82.6%. Adjusted net investment income surged to a record $1.9 billion. Overseas General expanded 6.7%, with Latin America jumping 11.7%, Asia advancing 7.5% and Europe climbing about 7%. North America personal lines rose 5.3%, although North America commercial slipped 2.7%.

Book value per share ended the period at $191.43, with tangible book value per share at $126.96. Core operating return on equity was 14.9%, while annualized core operating return on tangible equity reached 21.6%.

Outlook: The release gives no formal earnings or premium guidance, so attention turns to premium momentum, underwriting discipline, investment income and capital development. One expected item is the agreed sale involving USI Insurance Services, which is expected to result in a realized gain of $460 million on an investment of $740 million.

Capital One delivered net income of $3.0 billion, or $4.73 per diluted common share, while adjusted net income came to $5.81 per diluted common share.

The common equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 13.7%, while period-end total deposits were $484.3 billion.
Outlook: The release gives no formal guidance, so the focus remains on the Discover integration, the sustainability of revenue and margin momentum, expense discipline, credit-loss trends and capital strength.

# Cisco Q4 FY2026 Earnings Summary

Cisco closed fiscal 2026 with fourth-quarter revenue of **$17.3 billion**, a result that climbed **18%** year over year, while non-GAAP earnings per share reached **$1.22**.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Product revenue jumped **24%** year over year, while services revenue was flat.
- Revenue rose **18%** in the Americas, **19%** in EMEA and **14%** in APJC.
- Networking revenue surged **28%**, and total product orders climbed **35%** year over year.

**Profitability**
- GAAP operating income grew to **$4.3 billion**, up **38%**, for a GAAP operating margin of **24.7%**.
- Non-GAAP operating income advanced to **$6.2 billion**, with a non-GAAP operating margin of **35.9%**.
- GAAP earnings per share came in at **$0.97** for the quarter.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- Cash flow from operating activities rose to **$5.4 billion**, an increase of **27%** year over year.
- The company returned **$3.2 billion** to stockholders through share buybacks and dividends during the quarter.
- A quarterly dividend of **$0.42** per common share was declared.

**Outlook**
- For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue is expected to be **$18.0 billion** to **$18.2 billion**.
- For fiscal 2027, revenue is expected to be **$72.2 billion** to **$73.4 billion**.

**Bottom Line**
The company exited fiscal 2026 with strong revenue and order momentum, expanding operating income and solid operating cash flow, and guided for further revenue growth in fiscal 2027.

# Cognizant Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

Cognizant delivered revenue growth and stronger adjusted profitability in the third quarter, supported by solid performance in Financial Services and continued cash generation.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Revenue climbed to **$5.7 billion**, rising **4.6%** year-over-year, or **4.8%** in constant currency.
- Financial Services revenue grew **12%** year-over-year.

**Profitability**
- Operating margin came in at **15.4%**, while Adjusted Operating Margin expanded to **16.3%**, up **30 basis points** year-over-year.
- GAAP EPS surged to **$1.39**, up **148%** year-over-year.
- Adjusted EPS advanced to **$1.49**, increasing **7.2%** year-over-year.

**Bookings and Operations**
- Trailing 12-month bookings reached **$28.7 billion**, climbing **4%** year-over-year.
- Third quarter bookings slipped **7%** year-over-year.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- The company generated **$1.6 billion** of free cash flow year-to-date.
- Share repurchases totaled **$258 million** during the third quarter.
- A quarterly cash dividend of **$0.33** per share was declared in October.

**Outlook**
- Fourth quarter revenue is expected to be **$5.49 billion** to **$5.57 billion**.
- Full-year revenue is expected to be **$22.05 billion** to **$22.14 billion**.
- Full-year Adjusted Operating Margin is now expected to be approximately **16.1%**.
- Full-year Adjusted Diluted EPS guidance was revised to **$5.72** to **$5.79**.

**Bottom Line**
The quarter combined steady revenue growth, adjusted margin expansion and higher adjusted earnings, while the updated outlook points to continued growth and profitability improvement for the full year.

CVS Health Second-Quarter Profit Rises as Revenue and Adjusted Operating Income Grow
CVS Health reported second-quarter GAAP diluted EPS of $2.31, up from $0.80 in the prior year, while adjusted EPS climbed to $2.58 from $1.81. Total revenues rose 7.3% compared with the prior year, with growth across all operating segments.
Operating income jumped 97.5%, while adjusted operating income surged 35.4%. The company said the operating income increase reflected higher adjusted operating income and the absence of $833 million in legacy litigation charges recorded in the prior year.
In Health Care Benefits, total revenues grew 3.5%, driven by an increase in the Government business and partly offset by the exit of the individual exchange business in 2026. Adjusted operating income in the segment leaped 85.5%, helped by improved underlying performance in the Government business and the absence of a $471 million premium deficiency reserve recorded in the prior year. The medical benefit ratio slipped to 87.4% from 89.9%, and medical membership was 26.0 million as of June 30, 2026.
Health Services total revenues climbed 11.5%, while adjusted operating income rose 10.0%. Pharmacy claims processed were consistent on a 30-day equivalent basis. In Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness, total revenues increased slightly and adjusted operating income grew 10.2%, while prescriptions filled rose 4.3% on a 30-day equivalent basis.
CVS raised its full-year 2026 GAAP diluted EPS, adjusted EPS and cash flow from operations guidance, citing increases in the Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segments. The company said it was maintaining a cautious view for the remainder of the year amid continued elevated cost trends and the potential for macro headwinds. Prior years' health care costs payable estimates developed favorably by $1.2 billion during the six months ended June 30, 2026, and days claims payable were 41.7 days as of June 30, 2026.
As of June 30, 2026, the company had approximately 9,000 retail pharmacy locations, more than 1,000 walk-in and primary care medical clinics and a pharmacy benefits manager with approximately 87 million plan members.

source_block:
[s1] Second quarter GAAP diluted EPS of $2.31 increased from $0.80 in the prior year.
[s2] Adjusted EPS of $2.58 increased from $1.81 in the prior year, primarily due to improved adjusted operating income in the Health Care Benefits segment, reflecting continued execution on the Health Care Benefits segment margin recovery plan.
[s3] The Company is increasing its full-year 2026 GAAP diluted EPS, Adjusted EPS and cash flow from operations guidance to reflect increases in the Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segments, while maintaining a cautious view for the remainder of the year in light of continued elevated cost trends and the potential for macro headwinds.
[s4] For the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year:
[s5] Total revenues increased 7.3% driven by revenue growth across all operating segments.
[s6] Operating income increased 97.5% primarily due to the increase in adjusted operating income described below and the absence of $833 million in legacy litigation charges recorded in the prior year.
[s7] Adjusted operating income increased 35.4% driven by increases across all operating segments. See pages 3 through 5 for additional discussion of the adjusted operating income performance of the Company’s segments.
[s8] CVS Health launched a comprehensive approach to GLP-1 support across its CVS Pharmacy® and MinuteClinic® locations. New offerings include expanded pharmacy support designed to help patients access these treatments and stay on them, and a new $29 MinuteClinic virtual visit that connects eligible adults with licensed clinicians who can evaluate and, where clinically appropriate, prescribe GLP-1 therapy. In addition, CVS Pharmacy participates in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program, which runs through December 31, 2027. Eligible Medicare beneficiaries can access certain GLP-1 medications for $50 per month, offering more predictable and affordable pricing for patients who qualify.
[s9] CVS Caremark updated its most common commercial formularies, expanding GLP-1 options for members, building on its industry-leading efforts to help patients get FDA-approved weight management medications at an affordable cost.
[s10] Aetna launched its second generation Aetna Claims Assist Manager (“CAM”), an AI-powered agentic claims advisor platform designed to streamline claims processing and improve payment accuracy. CAM reduces processing time by over 20% for complex claims that require manual review, helping providers get paid faster and more consistently.
[s11] The segment results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were as follows:
[s12] Total revenues increased 3.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by an increase in the Government business, partially offset by a decline as a result of the Company’s exit of the individual exchange business in 2026.
[s13] Adjusted operating income increased 85.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by improved underlying performance in the Government business and the absence of a $471 million premium deficiency reserve recorded within the Group Medicare Advantage product line in the prior year.
[s14] The MBR decreased to 87.4% in the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 89.9% in the prior year primarily driven by improved underlying performance in the Government business and the absence of the premium deficiency reserve recorded in the prior year.
[s15] Medical membership as of June 30, 2026 of 26.0 million remained consistent compared with March 31, 2026.
[s16] Prior years’ health care costs payable estimates developed favorably by $1.2 billion during the six months ended June 30, 2026.
[s17] Days claims payable were 41.7 days as of June 30, 2026, a decrease of 1.2 days compared to March 31, 2026.
[s18] The segment results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were as follows:
[s19] Total revenues increased 11.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by pharmacy drug mix and brand inflation, partially offset by continued pharmacy client price improvements.
[s20] Adjusted operating income increased 10.0% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by improved purchasing economics, pharmacy drug mix and modest improvement in the Company’s health care delivery business. These increases were partially offset by continued pharmacy client price improvements.
[s21] Pharmacy claims processed remained consistent on a 30-day equivalent basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year.
[s22] The segment results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were as follows:
[s23] Total revenues increased slightly for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by pharmacy drug mix, increased prescription volume, including contributions from the Company’s Rite Aid asset acquisitions which were completed during the third quarter of 2025, and brand inflation. These increases were largely offset by regulatory-related price reductions on certain drugs, the impact of recent generic drug introductions and pharmacy reimbursement pressure.
[s24] Adjusted operating income increased 10.2% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by core pharmacy strength and contributions from the Company’s Rite Aid asset acquisitions. These increases were partially offset by continued business investments and the impact of consumer dynamics.
[s25] Prescriptions filled increased 4.3% on a 30-day equivalent basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily driven by incremental volume resulting from the Company’s Rite Aid prescription file acquisitions and increased utilization, partially offset by the absence of long-term care pharmacy prescription volume following the deconsolidation of Omnicare, LLC in September 2025.
[s26] As of June 30, 2026, the Company had approximately 9,000 retail pharmacy locations, more than 1,000 walk-in and primary care medical clinics and a leading pharmacy benefits manager with approximately 87 million plan members.
[s27] The Company also serves an estimated 37 million people through a broad range of health insurance products and related services.
[s28] The Company will be holding a conference call today for investors at 8:00 a.m. (Eastern Time) to discuss its second quarter results.
[s29] See “Non-GAAP Financial Information” beginning on page 10 and endnotes beginning on page 20 for explanations of non-GAAP financial measures presented in this press release.
[s30] See pages 12 through 14 and page 19 for reconciliations of each non-GAAP financial measure used in this release to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
[s31] The Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 provides a safe harbor for forward-looking statements made by or on behalf of CVS Health Corporation.
[s32] Statements in this press release that are forward-looking include, but are not limited to, the full-year 2026 guidance information, Mr. Joyner’s quotation and the information included in the reconciliations and endnotes.
[s33] Actual results may differ materially from those contemplated by the forward-looking statements due to the risks and uncertainties described in our Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) filings, including those set forth in the Risk Factors section and under the heading “Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements” in our most recently filed Annual Report on Form 10-K, our Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the quarterly periods ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and our Current Reports on Form 8-K.
[s34] Investor Contact: Larry McGrath | Executive Vice President, Capital Markets | (800) 201-0938
[s35] Media Contact: Ethan Slavin | Executive Director, Corporate Communications | (860) 273-6095
(lead-in) For the periods covered in this press release, the following items are excluded from the non-GAAP financial measures described above, as applicable, because the Company believes they neither relate to the ordinary course of the Company’s business nor reflect the Company’s underlying business performance:
[s36] During the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the acquisition-related integration costs relate to the acquisitions of Signify Health, Inc. and Oak Street Health, Inc. The acquisition-related integration costs are reflected in operating expenses within the Corporate/Other segment.
[s37] During the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, the Company recorded legacy litigation charges related to two court decisions associated with its past business practices. The legacy litigation charges were reflected in operating expenses within the Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness and Health Services segments.
[s38] During the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, the loss on the wind down and sale of Accountable Care assets represents the pre-tax loss on the divestiture of the Company’s Medicare Shared Savings Program (“MSSP”) operations, as well as costs incurred in connection with the wind down of the Company’s ACO REACH operations. The loss on Accountable Care assets was reflected in operating expenses within the Health Services segment.
[s39] During the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, the office real estate optimization charges primarily relate to the abandonment of leased real estate and the related right-of-use assets and property and equipment in connection with the Company’s evaluation of corporate office real estate space. The office real estate optimization charges were reflected in operating expenses within each segment.
[s40] See endnotes (1) and (2) on page 20 for definitions of non-GAAP financial measures.
[s41] Reconciliations of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure are presented on pages 12 through 14 and page 19.
[s42] Actual results may differ materially from those contemplated by the forward-looking information for a number of reasons as described in our SEC filings, including those set forth in the Risk Factors section and under the heading “Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements” in our most recently filed Annual Report on Form 10-K and our most recently filed Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. See “Non-GAAP Financial Information” earlier in this press release and endnote (2) later in this press release for more information on how we calculate Adjusted EPS.
[s43] (1) The Company defines adjusted operating income as operating income (GAAP measure) excluding the impact of amortization of intangible assets, net realized capital gains or losses and other items, if any, that neither relate to the ordinary course of the Company’s business nor reflect the Company’s underlying business performance, such as acquisition-related integration costs, certain legacy litigation charges, losses on Accountable Care assets and office real estate optimization charges.
[s44] (2) GAAP diluted earnings per share and Adjusted EPS, respectively, are calculated by dividing net income attributable to CVS Health and adjusted income attributable to CVS Health by the Company’s weighted average diluted shares outstanding.
[s45] (3) Medical benefit ratio is calculated by dividing the Health Care Benefits segment’s health care costs by premium revenues and represents the percentage of premium revenues spent on medical benefits for the segment’s insured members.
[s46] (4) Medical membership represents the number of members covered by the Health Care Benefits segment’s insured and ASC medical products and related services at a specified point in time.
[s47] (5) Pharmacy claims processed represents the number of prescription claims processed through the Company’s pharmacy benefits manager and dispensed by either its retail network pharmacies or the Company’s mail and specialty pharmacies.
[s48] Prescriptions filled represents the number of prescriptions dispensed through the Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segment’s retail pharmacies and infusion services operations, as well as through the Omnicare long-term care pharmacies prior to their deconsolidation in September 2025.
[s49] (6) Includes an adjustment to convert 90-day prescriptions to the equivalent of three 30-day prescriptions.
[s50] (7) Days claims payable is calculated by dividing the Health Care Benefits segment’s health care costs payable at the end of each quarter by its average health care costs per day during such quarter.
[s51] (8) Gross profit is calculated as the segment’s total revenues less its cost of products sold, and, for the Health Services segment, health care costs.
[s52] (9) Same store sales and prescription volume represent the change in revenues and prescriptions filled in the Company’s retail pharmacy stores that have been operating for greater than one year and digital sales initiated online or through mobile applications and fulfilled through the Company’s distribution centers, expressed as a percentage that indicates the increase or decrease relative to the comparable prior period.

DoorDash reports record third-quarter results and Instacart deal

DoorDash, Inc. reported record results for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, as total orders climbed 28% to 993 million. Marketplace gross order value surged 36% to $33.9 billion, while revenue jumped 34% to $4.6 billion.

GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders rose 91% to $466 million. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 41% to $1,060 million, equal to 3.1% of Marketplace GOV.

Excluding Deliveroo, the company said total orders grew 17%, with Marketplace GOV up 23% and revenue also advancing 23%. It said growth in its U.S. restaurant category was driven by mature cohorts and new consumers, while U.S. grocery and retail Marketplace GOV grew at more than double the pace of the restaurant category.

DoorDash said restaurant reservations in existing U.S. geographies expanded over 340% from the prior quarter, with more than 10% coming from consumers who were new to the platform in the quarter. International marketplaces also posted accelerated growth in Marketplace GOV, supported by faster order growth at each of its international brands.

The company generated $994 million in net cash from operating activities and $787 million in free cash flow during the quarter.

DoorDash also announced a definitive agreement to acquire Instacart for $65.00 per share, representing an equity value of approximately $17 billion. The transaction is expected to close at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to Instacart stockholder approval, regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
name: DoorDash
source_block:
[s1] DoorDash Releases Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
[s2] SAN FRANCISCO—(BUSINESS WIRE)—DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
[s3] In Q3 2026, we generated new quarterly records across Marketplace GOV, revenue, and net income.
[s4] In the quarter, we drove continued growth in our membership1 programs, launched new products, added more selection, advanced our global technology platform, and continued to innovate in key new areas of our business, including merchant services, AI, and autonomy.
[s5] We are pleased with our execution through the first nine months of 2026 and excited about the contributions we are making to local economies.
[s6] Additionally, we announced a definitive agreement to acquire Maplebear Inc. ("Instacart") for $65.00 per share, payable in at least 75% cash and up to 25% DoorDash common stock, subject to election and proration mechanics.
[s7] We believe that, together with Instacart, our combined scale and complementary technologies will enable us to build the next generation of tools and services that will empower local merchants to thrive, provide more choice for consumers, and generate more opportunity for Dashers2 and shoppers using Instacart's platform ("Shoppers").
[s8] Third Quarter 2026 Key Financial Metrics
[s9] Total Orders increased 28% year-over-year (Y/Y) to 993 million.
[s10] Marketplace GOV increased 36% Y/Y to $33.9 billion.
[s11] Revenue increased 34% Y/Y to $4.6 billion.
[s12] GAAP net income attributable to DoorDash, Inc. common stockholders increased 91% Y/Y to $466 million.
[s13] Adjusted EBITDA increased 41% Y/Y to $1,060 million.
[s14] In Q3 2026, we grew Total Orders 28% Y/Y (17% Y/Y excluding the impact of Deliveroo), Marketplace GOV 36% Y/Y (23% Y/Y excluding the impact of Deliveroo), and revenue 34% Y/Y (23% Y/Y excluding the impact of Deliveroo).
[s15] In Q3 2026, net income attributable to our common stockholders was $466 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $1,060 million.
[s16] As a note, beginning in Q4 2026, we intend to stop disclosing quarterly results excluding Deliveroo, as this will represent the anniversary of the acquisition and our total company results will be largely comparable with the year-ago period.
[s17] In our U.S. restaurant category in Q3 2026, Y/Y growth in Marketplace GOV accelerated slightly compared to Q2 2026, despite a challenging Y/Y comparison due to strong growth in Q3 2025.
[s18] On a quarter-over-quarter (Q/Q) basis, Marketplace GOV in the U.S. restaurant category grew faster in Q3 2026 than in any third quarter since Q3 2020.
[s19] Growth in the U.S. restaurant category was driven by continued Y/Y growth in order rates3 among mature cohorts4 and accelerated Y/Y growth in new consumers.5 We continued to drive strong growth in U.S. DashPass paid memberships in Q3 2026, which helps reduce transactional friction for consumers.
[s20] Over the last two years, growth in DashPass has helped drive a 9% reduction in transaction fees per order in the U.S. restaurant category.
[s21] In our U.S. grocery and retail categories, Y/Y growth in Marketplace GOV in Q3 2026 remained strong, growing at more than double the pace of Y/Y growth in our U.S. restaurant category.
[s22] During the quarter, in our U.S. grocery and retail categories, we announced several new merchant partners, supporting broader selection for consumers, and we continued to drive improvements to affordability and quality, which helped drive continued double-digit Y/Y growth in order rates for nearly all mature cohorts in Q3 2026, as well as Y/Y growth in new consumers to our U.S. grocery and retail categories that was consistent with Y/Y growth in the first half of 2026.
[s23] We view the relatively consistent growth in our U.S. marketplace in Q3 2026, and over the last four years, as a positive signal of underlying demand trends and a reflection of our ability to continue producing increased value through product innovation.
[s24] A recent addition to our service in some cities is reservations and, during Q3 2026, restaurant reservations through our U.S. marketplace grew over 340% Q/Q in existing geographies, with more than 10% of reservations in Q3 2026 coming from consumers who were new to DoorDash in the quarter.6
[s25] In our international marketplaces, we drove accelerated Y/Y growth in Marketplace GOV in Q3 2026,7 supported by accelerated Y/Y growth in Total Orders at each of our international brands.
[s26] We believe these improvements helped enable us to drive strong topline performance in our international marketplaces in Q3 2026, with contributions to total profitability that exceeded our expectations entering the quarter.
[s27] The first nine months of 2026 was a period of excellent execution and solid financial performance.
[s28] DoorDash, Inc. and Instacart today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion.
[s29] Instacart stockholders will have the right to elect to receive, for each Instacart share: (i) $65.00 in cash, (ii) 0.3372 shares of DoorDash common stock, or (iii) a mix of $48.75 in cash and 0.0843 shares of DoorDash common stock, in each case, subject to a cap on the total stock consideration issuable by DoorDash equal to 25% of the aggregate consideration and certain proration mechanics.
[s30] The value of $65.00 per Instacart share represents a 26% premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22, 2026, the last trading day before media reports about a possible transaction.
[s31] As described above, Instacart stockholders may elect to receive cash, DoorDash common stock or a mix of cash and DoorDash common stock for each Instacart share, subject to a cap on the total stock consideration issuable by DoorDash equal to 25% of the aggregate consideration.
[s32] DoorDash has entered into a financing commitment letter with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. providing for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge loan facility in support of the debt component of the transaction, subject to satisfaction or waiver of certain customary conditions.
[s33] The transaction is expected to close in the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028, subject to approval by Instacart stockholders, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, other regulatory approvals, including in Canada and Israel, and other customary closing conditions.
[s34] Stockholders holding about 19% of Instacart's outstanding shares have agreed to vote in favor of the transaction.
[s35] When we manage inventory ourselves, we achieve 99%+ fulfillment accuracy.8 We also deliver more than 10 minutes faster on average,9 because the warehouse environment is optimized for delivery whereas a grocery store was never set up for delivery.
[s36] Over the past 14 years, Instacart has built a great brand that serves millions of consumers.
[s37] We expect this to be true on Day 1 (after close), as the combined reach will increase density across the grocery store network, helping increase delivery speed, lower fulfillment costs, and provide greater earning opportunities for Shoppers.
[s38] We’ve done this both with our U.S. restaurant marketplace, where our reinvestments into product innovation have continued to generate durable growth, and in our acquired businesses outside of the U.S. Most recently, we demonstrated this investment philosophy and approach at Deliveroo, which in Q3 2026, saw Total Orders grow at twice the Y/Y rate it did in Q3 2025 (pre-acquisition).
[s39] To this end, we see a multi-year path to $500 million or more of annual synergies, net of investments.
[s40] We expect to invest more than 100% of total synergies in the first year after close, followed by positive net synergies in year two and beyond.
[s41] In addition to offering grocers the best Day 1 and long-term products from the DoorDash and Instacart marketplaces, when we combine Instacart’s leading Enterprise software with our leading fulfillment services, we believe we can offer grocers an even more efficient logistics network and best-in-class first-party products, too.
(lead-in) Based on our current outlook and assuming a stock price consistent with recent trading levels, we expect:
[s42] 2026 stock-based compensation expense of approximately $1.2 billion.
[s43] 2026 depreciation and amortization expense of approximately $1.2 billion, inclusive of approximately $450 million of amortization of acquired intangible assets.
[s44] 2026 year-end timing for merchant payments compared to the end of 2025 is expected to reduce reported 2026 Free Cash Flow by between $700 million and $800 million.
[s45] The Y/Y increase in Total Orders in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by growth in the number of consumers and the acquisition of Deliveroo.
[s46] Excluding the acquisition of Deliveroo, Total Orders increased 17% Y/Y in Q3 2026.
[s47] The Y/Y increase in Marketplace GOV in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by growth in Total Orders and an increase in average order value10 on our Marketplaces.
[s48] Excluding the acquisition of Deliveroo, Marketplace GOV increased 23% Y/Y in Q3 2026.
[s49] The Y/Y increase in revenue in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by growth in Marketplace GOV.
[s50] Excluding Deliveroo, revenue increased 23% Y/Y in Q3 2026.
[s51] The Y/Y increase in GAAP cost of revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by increases in Total Orders.
[s52] As a percentage of Marketplace GOV, GAAP cost of revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, was 6.4% in Q3 2026, down from 6.7% in Q3 2025 and in line with 6.4% in Q2 2026.
[s53] The Y/Y increase in GAAP sales and marketing expense in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by increases in advertising expenses and personnel-related compensation expenses.
[s54] As a percentage of Marketplace GOV, GAAP sales and marketing expense was 2.3% in Q3 2026, in line with 2.3% in Q3 2025 and down from 2.5% in Q2 2026.
[s55] The Y/Y increase in GAAP research and development expense in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by increases in personnel-related compensation expenses and third-party software expenses.
[s56] As a percentage of Marketplace GOV, GAAP research and development expense was 1.5% in Q3 2026, up from 1.4% in Q3 2025 and down from 1.6% in Q2 2026.
[s57] The Y/Y increase in GAAP general and administrative expense in Q3 2026 was driven primarily by increases in personnel-related compensation expenses.
[s58] As a percentage of Marketplace GOV, GAAP general and administrative expense was 1.3% in Q3 2026, down from 1.6% in Q3 2025 and 1.6% in Q2 2026.
[s59] GAAP net income attributable to DoorDash, Inc. common stockholders was $466 million in Q3 2026, up from $244 million in Q3 2025 and $200 million in Q2 2026.
[s60] Adjusted EBITDA was $1,060 million in Q3 2026, up 41% from $754 million in Q3 2025 and up 16% from $914 million in Q2 2026.
[s61] Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Marketplace GOV was 3.1% in Q3 2026, up from 3.0% in Q3 2025 and 2.8% in Q2 2026.
[s62] In Q3 2026, we generated net cash provided by operating activities of $994 million and Free Cash Flow of $787 million, up from $871 million and $723 million, respectively, in Q3 2025.
[s63] In February 2025, our board of directors authorized the repurchase of up to $5.0 billion of our Class A common stock.
[s64] Year to date through October 28, we have repurchased a total of 6.8 million shares of our Class A common stock for $1.0 billion under the February 2025 authorization.
[s65] We currently have approximately $4.0 billion remaining under the current stock repurchase authorization.
[s66] DoorDash will host a conference call and webcast to discuss our quarterly results today at 5:30 a.m. Pacific Time (8:30 a.m. Eastern Time).
[s67] This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, which statements involve substantial risks and uncertainties.
[s68] Forward-looking statements in this release include, but are not limited to, our expectations regarding our financial position and financial and operating performance, including our outlook and guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026 and our assumptions underlying such guidance; our expectations regarding our stock-based compensation expense, our depreciation and amortization expense, and our Free Cash Flow; our expectations regarding the impact of year-end timing of merchant payments on 2026 Free Cash Flow; statements regarding the proposed acquisition of Instacart by DoorDash pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger among DoorDash, Ibiza Merger Sub, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of DoorDash, and Instacart (the "Merger Agreement" and such transaction, the "Proposed Transaction"); the expected financing of the Proposed Transaction; the expected timing and likelihood of completion of the Proposed Transaction on the terms contemplated or at all; the expected benefits, synergies, and strategic value of the Proposed Transaction, including the future financial and operating performance of the combined company; our plans and expectations regarding the integration of Instacart; and our plans, objectives, expectations, and intentions with respect to the Proposed Transaction, the period of pendency of the Proposed Transaction and the combined company; our priorities and our plans and expectations regarding our overall business strategy and investment approach; expectations regarding our focus to improve the efficiency of our operations and our capital allocation across our international marketplaces; [s1] Dollar General Corporation Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
[s2] Raises Financial Guidance for Fiscal Year 2026
[s3] GOODLETTSVILLE, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dollar General Corporation (NYSE: DG) today reported financial results for its second quarter (13 weeks) ended July 31, 2026.
[s4] Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights
[s5] Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Overview
[s6] Net sales increased 5.2% to $11.3 billion in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $10.7 billion in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s7] Same-store sales increased 3.5% compared to the second quarter of fiscal 2025, reflecting increases of 2.0% in customer traffic and 1.5% in average transaction amount.
[s8] Same-store sales in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 included growth in each of the consumables, seasonal, home products, and apparel categories.
[s9] Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 32.6% in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to 31.3% in the second quarter of fiscal 2025, an increase of 127 basis points.
[s10] The Company estimates the gross margin benefit of tariff refunds, after related reinvestments, was approximately 81 basis points.
[s11] Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (“SG&A”) as a percentage of net sales were essentially flat year over year, at 25.8% in both the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s12] The primary expense that was higher as a percentage of net sales in the second quarter of 2026 was depreciation and amortization; offset by rent, which was lower as a percentage of sales.
[s13] Operating profit for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 29.2% to $769.2 million compared to $595.4 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s14] The Company estimates the operating margin benefit of tariff refunds, after related reinvestments, was approximately 66 basis points.
[s15] Net interest expense for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased 25.7% to $42.9 million compared to $57.7 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s16] The effective income tax rate in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 was 24.2% compared to 23.5% in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s17] The Company reported net income of $550.3 million for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of 33.8% compared to $411.4 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
[s18] Diluted EPS increased 33.3% to $2.48 for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to diluted EPS of $1.86 in the second quarter of fiscal 2025, including an estimated benefit from tariff refunds, after related reinvestments, of approximately $0.25.
[s19] As of July 31, 2026, total merchandise inventories, at cost, were $6.6 billion compared to $6.6 billion as of August 1, 2025, a decrease of 2.7% on an average per-store basis.
[s20] Total additions to property and equipment in the 26-week period ended July 31, 2026 were $758 million, including approximately: $414 million for improvements, upgrades, remodels and relocations of existing stores; $168 million for distribution and transportation-related projects; $133 million related to store facilities, primarily for leasehold improvements, fixtures and equipment in new stores; and $31 million for information systems upgrades and technology-related projects.
[s21] During the second quarter of 2026, the Company opened 125 new stores in the United States and one new store in Mexico, remodeled 665 stores through Project Renovate and 711 stores through Project Elevate, and relocated 5 stores.
[s22] The Company intends to repurchase shares under its existing share repurchase program in the second half of the fiscal year ending January 29, 2027 (“fiscal 2026”).
[s23] The Company’s total remaining authorization for future repurchases was $1.4 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026.
[s24] Under the authorization, repurchases may be made from time to time in open market transactions, including pursuant to trading plans adopted in accordance with Rule 10b5-1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or in privately negotiated transactions.
[s25] On August 26, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.59 per share on the Company’s common stock, payable on or before October 20, 2026 to shareholders of record on October 6, 2026.
[s26] Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Guidance and Store Growth Outlook
[s27] The Company does not anticipate a material impact to its financial results from tariff refunds, after related reinvestments, in the second half of fiscal 2026.

[s29] The Company continues to expect capital expenditures, including those related to investments in the Company’s strategic initiatives, in the range of $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.

Quest Diagnostics Raises Full-Year Outlook After Third-Quarter Growth

Quest Diagnostics reported third quarter revenues of $3.10 billion, climbing 10.0% from 2025 on strong organic revenue growth. Reported diluted earnings per share reached $2.78, surging 28.7% from 2025, while adjusted diluted EPS grew to $3.00, up 15.4%.

The company raised its outlook for the full year 2026, with revenues now expected to be between $12.065 billion and $12.105 billion. Reported diluted EPS for the full year is now expected to be between $10.21 and $10.31, and adjusted diluted EPS is expected to be between $11.25 and $11.35.

Quest also announced expanded offerings and initiatives during the quarter, including a tailored lab test panel with over 50 biomarkers that iPhone and iPad users in the United States can purchase directly through the Apple Health app, available to the public later this year. The company extended its AD-Detect menu and advanced Project Nova to the solutions-build phase, with Epic solutions expected to be deployed in its first lab in the fall of 2027.

The company said it will hold its 2027 Investor Day on March 25, 2027, at the New York Stock Exchange. Quest serves half the physicians and hospitals in the United States and one in three adult Americans each year, with nearly 60,000 employees.

For its adjusted outlook, Quest noted estimated pre-tax charges of $20 million primarily tied to workforce reductions and integration costs, estimated pre-tax amortization expenses of $149 million, and estimated pre-tax net losses of $9 million linked to the contingent consideration accrual. Income tax impacts for those items were primarily calculated using a combined statutory income tax rate of 25.5%.

Disney Q1 Fiscal 2026: Top-Line Growth, Softer Segment Profit
Revenue growth outpaced profitability in the quarter, as stronger Experiences and Entertainment sales were offset by higher costs.

Revenue rose 5% to $26.0 billion, while income before income taxes came in at $3.7 billion. Total segment operating income declined 9% to $4.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.34, and adjusted EPS was $1.63.

Entertainment revenue climbed 7%, but operating income fell to $1.1 billion, leaving an Entertainment segment operating margin of 9.5%. SVOD revenue grew 11%, with SVOD operating income reaching $450 million and SVOD operating margin at 8.4%. Sports generated segment operating income of $191 million, including an adverse impact of approximately $110 million from the temporary suspension of YouTube TV carriage.

Experiences delivered record quarterly revenue of $10.0 billion and segment operating income of $3.3 billion. Domestic Parks & Experiences operating income rose 8%, while attendance at domestic parks was up 1%. Cash provided by operations dropped to $0.7 billion, and capital expenditures increased to $3.0 billion.

Outlook: For Q2 fiscal 2026, the company expects Entertainment segment operating income comparable to Q2 fiscal 2025 and SVOD operating income of approximately $500 million, while Sports segment operating income is expected to decline by $100 million on comparable revenue. For fiscal 2026, it guided to double-digit Entertainment segment operating income growth, a SVOD operating margin of 10%, low-single-digit Sports segment operating income growth, high-single-digit Experiences segment operating income growth, and double-digit adjusted EPS growth. It also expects $19 billion in cash provided by operations and remains on track to repurchase $7 billion of stock.

Second-Quarter Profit Climbs on Higher Revenue and Airfreight Tonnage

Expeditors International reported higher second-quarter results, with revenue and profit advancing as airfreight volumes strengthened. Revenues rose 32% to $3.5 billion, operating income climbed 41% to $350 million, and net earnings attributable to shareholders grew 45% to $266 million. Diluted net earnings attributable to shareholders per share jumped 51% to $2.03.

Airfreight tonnage increased 14% from a year earlier, while ocean container volume remained flat. Tonnage also rose 16% compared with the first quarter of 2026, helped by trade lanes including Asia-U.S. and Asia-Europe. Volumes advanced 7% compared with the first quarter of 2026.

The companys results included a $25 million pretax restructuring charge related to its Global Technology team. Expeditors said the restructuring is expected to lower its cost structure by approximately $50 million annually, equating to nearly 10% of total corporate overhead expenses. The charge was partly offset by a $16 million gain on the sale of an underutilized property during the quarter.

Operating efficiency improved to 32.2% in the second quarter, inclusive of the restructuring charge. The company said second-quarter headcount remained essentially flat versus the first quarter of 2026, with reductions tied to the restructuring mainly expected to be realized in the third quarter.

Expeditors returned $461 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the second quarter, bringing the total for the first half of 2026 to $748 million. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the company repurchased 2.3 million shares at an average price of $151.50.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Expeditors repurchased 4.3 million shares at an average price of $148.87. The company also plans an Investor Day in New York City in November 2026 for shareholders and analysts.

Fastenal Q3 2026: Broad Sales Strength With Operating Leverage
Fastenal posted a strong third quarter as share gains with larger customers, pricing actions and broad-based demand across core end markets lifted sales and profits.

Daily sales rose 15.5% year-over-year, while net sales climbed $330.0, also 15.5%, compared with the prior-year quarter. Product pricing added approximately 240 basis points to net sales growth, and direct materials outpaced indirect materials amid greater fastener contribution and continued strength with manufacturing customers. Contract customers continued to outperform, and the company signed 7,484 weighted FASTBin and FASTVend devices during the quarter.

Profitability reflected a mix of gross-margin pressure and expense leverage. Gross profit slipped to 44.8% of net sales from 45.3%, as a shift toward larger customers and price/cost weighed on results. SG&A expenses improved to 23.3% of net sales from 24.6%, lifting operating income to 21.5% of net sales from 20.7%. Net income jumped 19.7% to $401.6, with diluted net income per share advancing to $0.35 from $0.29.

Cash generation remained solid, with net cash provided by operating activities growing to $421.6 and representing 105.0% of net income. Fastenal returned $328.4 to shareholders, or 81.8% of net income, comprising dividends of $298.2 and share repurchases of $30.2.

Outlook: Fastenal lowered its goal for weighted FASTBin and FASTVend device signings to between 27,000 and 29,000 MEUs and continues to expect investment in property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales, of between $310.0 and $330.0, alongside elevated IT spending.
