[s1] Fastenal Company Reports 2026 Third Quarter Earnings
[s2] Daily sales increased 15.5% year-over-year, primarily driven by share gains with larger customers, pricing actions, and broad-based demand across core end markets.
[s3] Operating margin was 21.5%, a 90 basis point improvement year-over-year, as selling, general, and administrative expense leverage more than offset customer mix-related gross margin pressure.
[s4] Operating cash flow was $422 million, representing 105% of net income, reflecting the timing of working capital changes associated with strong sales growth.
[s5] Returned $328 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, representing 82% of net income.
[s6] WINONA, Minn., October 14, 2026 (BUSINESS WIRE) -- Fastenal Company (Nasdaq:FAST) ('Fastenal,' 'we,' 'our,' or 'us'), a global leader in supply chain services, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.
[s7] Net sales increased $330.0, or 15.5%, in the third quarter of 2026 when compared to the third quarter of 2025 (both periods had the same number of business days).
[s8] Sales performance reflects the contribution from improved customer contract signings since the first quarter of 2024, product pricing, and a modest improvement in industrial production in the first nine months of 2026.
[s9] Foreign exchange rates negatively impacted sales growth by approximately 10 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025 when foreign exchange rates contributed approximately 10 basis points to sales growth.
[s10] The impact of product pricing on net sales in the third quarter of 2026 was an increase of approximately 240 basis points, compared to an increase of 240 to 270 basis points in the third quarter of 2025.
[s11] Beginning in the fourth quarter of 2025, we expanded our reporting to provide a more comprehensive view of direct (original equipment manufacturing/production) and indirect (maintenance, repair, and operations/facilities maintenance) business across product categories.
[s12] During the third quarter of 2026, direct materials outpaced indirect materials, reflecting greater contribution from fastener sales and continued strength with manufacturing customers.
[s13] From a customer standpoint, we have two categories: 1) contracts, which include national multi-site, local and regional, and government customers with significant revenue potential, and 2) non-contracts.
[s14] Sales with our contract customers continue to outperform as we realize incremental sales from implementing customer signings that we have achieved since the first quarter of 2024.
[s15] Our strategy prioritizes customer Sites with monthly sales potential of $50,000 or more.
[s16] (1)Sites represent the number of customer locations served by our network.
[s17] (2)Sites numbers reflect the monthly average of active Site counts.
[s18] (3)Monthly sales per Site totals are not rounded to the millions and represent the exact dollar amount.
[s19] (4)$50k+ Sites are disclosed as a representation of Onsite-like customers and are also a subset of $10k+ and $5k+ Sites.
[s20] (5)Other sales represent sales to Sites under $5k per month and sales that are not tied to a specific Site.
[s21] We signed 7,484 weighted FASTBin and FASTVend devices in the third quarter of 2026.
[s22] Our goal for weighted FASTBin and FASTVend device signings in 2026 is between 27,000 and 29,000 MEUs (our previous goal was between 28,000 and 30,000 MEUs).
[s23] The table below summarizes signings and installations of our FMI devices and sales through our FMI devices, eBusiness (1) tools, and Digital Footprint (2).
[s24] (1)Our eBusiness includes eProcurement activities, which are integrated transactions, including electronic data interchange (EDI), and eCommerce (transactional website sales).
[s25] (2)Digital Footprint is a combination of our sales through FMI (FASTStock, FASTBin, and FASTVend) plus that portion of our eBusiness sales that does not represent billings of FMI services.
[s26] (3)Weighted FASTBin/FASTVend signings and installations reflect the percent change compared to the same period in the prior year.
[s27] Gross profit, as a percentage of net sales, decreased approximately 40 basis points to 44.8% in the third quarter of 2026 from 45.3% in the third quarter of 2025.
[s28] A continued shift in customer mix toward larger customers reduced gross margin by approximately 50 basis points.
[s29] Price/cost reduced gross margin by approximately 30 basis points, an improvement of approximately 10 basis points from the second quarter of 2026.
[s30] Approximately 20 basis points of the benefit reflected favorable timing.
[s31] Our gross margin decreased approximately 75 basis points in the second quarter of 2026 to 44.6% of net sales, from 45.3% in the second quarter of 2025.
[s32] Gross margin improved from the second quarter of 2026 to the third quarter of 2026.
[s33] SG&A expenses, as a percentage of net sales, were 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026 versus 24.6% in the third quarter of 2025, an improvement of 130 basis points.
[s34] Employee-related expenses, which typically represent 70% to 75% of total SG&A expenses, improved 90 basis points as a percentage of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025.
[s35] Occupancy-related expenses, which typically represent 14% to 19% of total SG&A expenses, improved 50 basis points as a percentage of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven mainly by fixed cost leverage.
[s36] Combined, all other SG&A expenses, which typically represent 10% to 15% of total SG&A expenses, increased 10 basis points as a percentage of net sales when compared to the third quarter of 2025.
[s37] Operating income as a percentage of net sales increased to 21.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 20.7% in the third quarter of 2025.
[s38] Net interest income was $0.4 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to net interest expense of $0.9 in the third quarter of 2025, primarily from lower debt balances.
[s39] We recorded income tax expense of $129.6 in the third quarter of 2026, or 24.4% of income before income taxes.
[s40] Income tax expense was $105.1 in the third quarter of 2025, or 23.9% of income before income taxes.
[s41] We believe our ongoing tax rate, absent any discrete tax items or broader changes to tax law, will be approximately 24.6%.
[s42] Net income was $401.6 in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 19.7% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
[s43] Diluted net income per share was $0.35 compared to $0.29 in the third quarter of 2025.
[s44] Net cash provided by operating activities was $421.6 in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 9.0% from the third quarter of 2025.
[s45] Cash flow from operations represented 105.0% of net income, compared to 115.3% in the third quarter of 2025 and our five-year third quarter average of 101.1%.
[s46] Net cash provided by operating activities was $1,065.7 in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 14.9% from the first nine months of 2025, representing 94.8% of net income versus 96.2% in the first nine months of 2025 and the most recent five-year average of 96.4%.
[s47] The dollar and percentage change in accounts receivable, net, inventories, and accounts payable as of September 30, 2026 when compared to September 30, 2025 were as follows:
[s48] The increase in our accounts receivable balance in the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to sales growth, including relative growth with larger customers that tend to carry longer payment terms.
[s49] The slight increase in our inventory balance in the third quarter of 2026, despite double-digit sales growth, reflects disciplined inventory management.
[s50] The increase in our accounts payable balance in the third quarter of 2026 was mainly attributable to an increase in inventory spending to support growth.
[s51] During the third quarter of 2026, our investment in property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales, was $71.8 (2.9% of net sales), which was an increase from $54.7 (2.6% of net sales) in the third quarter of 2025.
[s52] Our five- and ten-year annual average as a percent of net sales was 2.5% and 3.1%, respectively.
[s53] For 2026, we continue to expect our investment in property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales, to be between $310.0 and $330.0, an increase from $230.6 in 2025.
[s54] Second, we expect elevated IT spending as projects that were expected in 2025 experienced delays and are expected to continue throughout 2026.
[s55] During the third quarter of 2026, we returned $328.4, or 81.8% of net income, to our shareholders in the form of dividends ($298.2) and share repurchases ($30.2), compared to the third quarter of 2025 when we returned $252.5, or 75.3% of net income, in the form of dividends.
[s56] Over the past five years, we have returned an average of 76.0% of net income to shareholders in the third quarter.
[s57] Total debt on our balance sheet was $100.0 at the end of the third quarter of 2026, or 2.4% of total capital (the sum of stockholders' equity and total debt), compared to $195.0, or 4.8% of total capital, at the end of the third quarter of 2025.
[s58] During the last twelve months, we increased our total full-time equivalent (FTE; based on 40 hours per week) employee headcount by 181.
[s59] Our total FTE selling personnel decreased by 82, primarily driven by a drop in hours worked by part-time selling personnel.
[s60] We increased our distribution and transportation FTE personnel by 105 to support increased product throughput at our distribution facilities.
[s61] We increased our remaining FTE personnel by 158, which related primarily to personnel investments in supply chain support.

Jacobs Solutions lifts full-year outlook as adjusted profit climbs

Jacobs Solutions reported fiscal third-quarter gross revenue of $4.1 billion, up 34.5% from a year earlier, while adjusted net revenue rose to $2.4 billion, an increase of 8.3%.

GAAP net earnings at the company slipped to $137.4 million from $181.2 million in the year-earlier quarter, with the result reflecting a temporarily higher tax rate associated with the PA acquisition transaction. GAAP earnings per share declined to $1.16 from $1.56, while adjusted earnings per share climbed 13.6% to $1.84 and adjusted EBITDA grew 16.7% to $366.8 million.

Backlog reached $28.9 billion, up 27.3% year over year. Jacobs posted a quarterly book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x, while its adjusted net revenue book-to-bill ratio was 1.1x.

The company generated $456 million in cash from operations during the quarter. It repurchased $142 million of its shares in the quarter, bringing year-to-date repurchases to $614 million.

Jacobs raised its fiscal 2026 guidance, forecasting adjusted net revenue growth of 9.5% to 10.0% and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.7% to 14.8%. The company now expects adjusted earnings per share of $7.20 to $7.30 and an adjusted free cash flow margin of approximately 8%.

J.B. Hunt posts higher third-quarter profit as revenue climbs 20%
J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc. reported third-quarter 2026 U.S. GAAP net earnings of $172.4 million, or diluted earnings per share of $1.82, compared with $170.8 million, or $1.76 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. Total operating revenue rose to $3.68 billion from $3.05 billion a year earlier, an increase of 20%.
Revenue excluding fuel surcharge revenue grew 13% from the year-earlier quarter. Operating income edged up 2% to $247.1 million from $242.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, while the effective income tax rate was 25.5%, versus 24.0% a year earlier.
In Intermodal, volume climbed 8% over the same period in 2025 and segment gross revenue jumped 20%. Revenue per load excluding fuel surcharge revenue rose 2% year over year, and segment operating income advanced 18%.
Dedicated Contract Services revenue increased 11%, helped by improved productivity. Integrated Capacity Solutions revenue surged 57% from the third quarter of 2025, and the segment swung to operating income of $9.6 million from an operating loss a year earlier.
Final Mile Services revenue slipped 3% from the same period in 2025. Truckload gross revenue climbed 37%, although segment operating income fell to $7.0 million.
At September 30, 2026, J.B. Hunt had approximately $1.12 billion outstanding on various debt instruments, compared with $1.60 billion at September 30, 2025. During the third quarter, the company purchased approximately 704,000 shares of common stock for approximately $174 million.

[s1] J.B. HUNT TRANSPORT SERVICES, INC. REPORTS U.S. GAAP REVENUES, NET EARNINGS AND EARNINGS PER SHARE FOR THE THIRD QUARTER 2026
[s2] LOWELL, Ark., October 15, 2026 - J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc., (NASDAQ: JBHT) announced third quarter 2026 U.S. GAAP (United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) net earnings of $172.4 million, or diluted earnings per share of $1.82 versus third quarter 2025 net earnings of $170.8 million, or $1.76 per diluted share.
[s3] Total operating revenue for the current quarter was $3.68 billion compared with $3.05 billion for the third quarter 2025, an increase of 20%.
[s4] Current quarter total operating revenue, excluding fuel surcharge revenue, increased 13% versus the third quarter 2025.
[s5] The increase in revenue, excluding fuel surcharge revenue, was primarily driven by an 8% increase in Intermodal (JBI) loads, a 27% increase in Integrated Capacity Solutions (ICS) revenue per load, excluding fuel surcharge revenue, and a 29% increase in Truckload (JBT) revenue per load, excluding fuel surcharge revenue, partially offset by a 10% decline in Final Mile Services (FMS) stops.
[s6] Operating income for the current quarter increased 2% to $247.1 million versus $242.7 million for the third quarter 2025.
[s7] Net interest expense for the current quarter decreased compared to third quarter 2025 due to a lower average consolidated debt balance partially offset by a modestly higher average interest rate
[s8] The effective income tax rate in the current quarter was 25.5% versus 24.0% in the third quarter 2025 due to the timing of certain discrete tax items.
[s9] We expect our 2026 full year annual tax rate to be approximately 24.0%.
[s10] Intermodal volume increased 8% over the same period in 2025.
[s11] Transcontinental network loads increased 1%, while Eastern network loads increased 18% compared to the third quarter 2025.
[s12] Segment gross revenue increased 20% from the prior-year period, reflecting an 11% increase in gross revenue per load, resulting from higher fuel surcharge revenue, customer rates and changes in mix of freight, and the 8% increase in volume.
[s13] Revenue per load excluding fuel surcharge revenue increased 2% year-over-year.
[s14] Operating income increased 18% compared to the prior year period in the third quarter primarily from improved network balance and efficiency improvements, continued discipline and execution on our initiative to lower our cost to serve and lower container storage expense.
[s15] DCS revenue increased 11% during the current quarter over the same period 2025 driven by a 10% improvement in productivity (revenue per truck per week) and a 1% increase in average trucks.
[s16] Productivity excluding fuel surcharge revenue increased 3% from a year ago driven by contracted indexed-based price escalators and a decline in idled tractor equipment.
[s17] On a net basis, there were 162 additional revenue producing trucks in the fleet by the end of the quarter compared to the prior-year period and 120 more versus the end of the second quarter 2026.
[s18] Customer retention rates remain at approximately 96%.
[s19] Operating income decreased 22% from the prior-year quarter.
[s20] ICS revenue increased 57% during the current quarter versus the third quarter 2025.
[s21] Overall segment volume increased 22% versus the prior-year period with growth in both published and spot volume.
[s22] Revenue per load increased 29% compared to the third quarter 2025 due to increases in both contractual and transactional rates.
[s23] Contractual volume represented approximately 63% of the total load volume and 58% of the total revenue in the current quarter compared to 63% and 64%, respectively, in third quarter 2025.
[s24] Operating income was $9.6 million compared to an operating loss of $0.8 million in the third quarter 2025.
[s25] Gross profit margin of 14.3% in the third quarter of 2026 declined compared to 15.0% in the prior year period but improved from 12.5% in the second quarter of 2026.
[s26] FMS revenue decreased 3% compared to the same period 2025.
[s27] Operating income decreased 76% compared to the prior-year period primarily driven by the decline in segment revenue along with higher purchased transportation expense.
[s28] JBT segment gross revenue increased 37% compared to the same period in the previous year.
[s29] Segment gross revenue excluding fuel surcharge revenue increased 34% driven by a 29% increase in gross revenue per load excluding fuel surcharge revenue and a 4% increase in load volume.
[s30] Total average effective trailer count decreased by approximately 60 units, or 1% versus the prior-year period.
[s31] Compared to the third quarter 2025, trailer turns in the quarter were up 3%, primarily due to better network balance, improved asset utilization and modestly higher load volume.
[s32] JBT segment operating income decreased 6% to $7.0 million versus the third quarter 2025.
[s33] At September 30, 2026, we had approximately $1.12 billion outstanding on various debt instruments compared to $1.60 billion at September 30, 2025 and $1.47 billion at December 31, 2025.
[s34] Our net capital expenditures for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 approximated $291.1 million compared to $490.9 million for the same period 2025.
[s35] At September 30, 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $4 million.
[s36] In the third quarter 2026, we purchased approximately 704,000 shares of common stock for approximately $174 million.
[s37] At September 30, 2026, we had approximately $619 million remaining under our share repurchase authorization.
[s38] Actual shares outstanding at September 30, 2026 approximated 93.2 million.
[s39] The company will hold a conference call today from 4:00–5:00 p.m. CDT to discuss the quarterly earnings.
[s40] Please log on 15 minutes early to register, download and install any necessary audio software.
[s41] Actual results may differ materially from those currently anticipated due to a number of factors, including, but not limited to, those discussed in Item 1A of our Annual Report filed on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Lumentum Q4 Fiscal 2026: Revenue Crosses $1 Billion
Adjusted profitability expanded sharply as revenue climbed, even as a one-time non-cash debt charge drove a large GAAP loss.

Revenue reached $1.01 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, up from $808.4 million in the third quarter and $480.7 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025. Management cited broad-based traction, with OCS solutions and the cloud module business, including advancing 1.6T adoption, beginning to layer in as growth drivers.

GAAP gross margin was 47.4%, while non-GAAP gross margin was 50.4%. GAAP operating margin came in at 27.8%, compared with non-GAAP operating margin of 36.6%. The GAAP net loss was $7.2 billion, or $84.65 per diluted share, driven by a one-time, non-cash loss on debt extinguishment of $7.8 billion tied to the equitization of certain convertible notes. On a non-GAAP basis, net income rose to $326.3 million, or $3.23 per diluted share, from $225.7 million, or $2.37 per diluted share, in the third quarter.

Lumentum held $2.7 billion in total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments at quarter end. That balance declined by $433.9 million from the end of the third quarter, while increasing by $1.9 billion from the end of fiscal year 2025.

Outlook: For the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, Lumentum expects net revenue of $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion, with a guidance midpoint of $1.25 billion, non-GAAP operating margin of 39.5% to 40.5%, and non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $4.05 to $4.35.

Lilly (Eli) said first-quarter revenue rose 45% to $12.73 billion, helped by a 53% increase in volume.
Revenue in the U.S. climbed 49% to $8.49 billion, while revenue outside the U.S. grew 38% to $4.24 billion.
Worldwide Mounjaro revenue jumped 113% to $3.84 billion, and U.S. Zepbound revenue reached $2.31 billion. Worldwide Verzenio revenue advanced 10% to $1.16 billion.
Gross margin surged to $10.50 billion and was 82.5% of revenue. Research and development expenses rose to $2.73 billion, while marketing, selling and administrative expenses increased to $2.47 billion.
The company recorded acquired in-process research and development charges of $1.57 billion. Net income was $2.76 billion, with earnings per share of $3.06 on a reported basis and $3.34 on a non-GAAP basis.
Lilly reaffirmed its revenue guidance of between $58.0 billion and $61.0 billion, while guidance for earnings per share decreased to a range of $20.17 to $21.67 on a reported basis.

Masco: Margin Expansion Lifts Earnings
Strong operating execution drove solid earnings growth on modest sales gains in the third quarter.
Revenue rose 3 percent to $1,966 million, while net sales climbed 4 percent excluding the divestiture and currency impacts. Plumbing Products net sales grew 4 percent, or 5 percent in local currency and excluding the divestiture. In local currency, North American net sales increased 5 percent, while International net sales slipped 5 percent, or 1 percent excluding the divestiture.
Profitability improved markedly, with gross margin reaching 36.6 percent and operating profit totaling $338 million. Operating profit margin was 17.2 percent, while adjusted operating profit margin expanded to 17.9 percent. Earnings per share were $1.17, and adjusted earnings per share grew 23 percent to $1.19 per share.
Cash generation supported continued capital returns, with $322 million returned to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in the quarter. Liquidity at the end of the third quarter was $1,610 million, including availability under the revolving credit facility. The board also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.32 per share.
Outlook: For 2026, the company expects earnings per share in the range of $4.51 to $4.61 per share, and adjusted earnings per share of $4.65 to $4.75 per share, raised from previous adjusted guidance of $4.40 to $4.60 per share.

[s1] Meta Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
[s2] MENLO PARK, Calif. – October 21, 2026 – Meta Platforms, Inc. (Nasdaq: META) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
[s3] Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights
[s4] In August 2026, we announced an agreement with 52 attorneys general to resolve litigation related to teen mental health and social media, which provides for payments of up to approximately $18.59 billion.
[s5] Third quarter 2026 costs and expenses includes a $9.89 billion charge related to this agreement.
[s6] Excluding this charge, the third quarter 2026:
[s7] Income from operations of $12.99 billion would have increased by $9.89 billion to $22.88 billion.
[s8] Diluted EPS of $3.83 would have increased by $3.57 to $7.40.
[s9] Effective tax rate of 24% would have decreased by 7 percentage points to 17%.
[s10] Third Quarter 2026 Operational and Other Financial Highlights
[s11] Family daily active people (DAP) – DAP was 3.64 billion on average for September 2026, an increase of 3% year-over-year.
[s12] Ad impressions – Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps increased by 10% year-over-year.
[s13] Average price per ad – Average price per ad increased by 14% year-over-year.
[s14] Revenue – Revenue was $64.60 billion, an increase of 26% year-over-year on both a reported and constant currency basis.
[s15] Costs and expenses – Total costs and expenses were $51.61 billion, an increase of 68% year-over-year. This includes the litigation charge as discussed above.
[s16] Capital expenditures – Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.91 billion.
[s17] Capital return program – Dividend and dividend equivalent payments were $1.36 billion.
[s18] Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities – Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $82.45 billion as of September 30, 2026.
[s19] Cash flow – Cash flow from operating activities was $32.79 billion, and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion.(1)
[s20] Headcount – Headcount was 66,775 as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of 15% year-over-year.
[s21] (1) For more information on our free cash flow non-GAAP financial measure, see the sections entitled "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results" in this press release.
[s22] We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion.
[s23] Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.
[s24] We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in the third quarter.
[s25] We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.
[s26] Excluding the third quarter legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.
[s27] At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.
[s28] We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.
[s29] Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 2026 tax rate to be between 15-17%.
[s30] Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives.
[s31] Looking ahead, although we are not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.
[s32] Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability and expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment toward other priority areas, primarily AI.
[s33] The Board of Directors has approved the establishment of a new class of publicly listed, non-voting Class C common stock, with an effective date in January 2027.
(lead-in) The Special Committee and the Board determined that creating this new class of stock is advisable, fair, and in the best interests of Meta and its shareholders for a number of reasons, including:
[s34] Continuing to Maximize Long-Term Value for All Shareholders – Since Meta's formation, its management team has prioritized long-term goals and value creation, and its stock price has increased by more than 1,700% since its IPO. By contrast, over the same period, the S&P 500 has increased approximately 495%. The Special Committee wants Meta to continue innovating with an emphasis on long-term growth, which the creation of the Class C stock is intended to help facilitate.
[s35] Meta intends to file an amended and restated certificate of incorporation in Delaware to establish the Class C common stock, with an effective date of January 19, 2027.
[s36] More information will be available in our Report on Form 8-K and information statement to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

[s2] Second-Quarter Revenues Increase 21% to New Record
[s3] Operational Efficiency Opportunities Expected to Drive $350 Million of Cash Flow Benefits
[s4] Raises Full-Year 2026 Revenues Guidance and Reaffirms Adjusted EBITDA Guidance
[s5] RALEIGH, N.C. (July 30, 2026) – Martin Marietta Materials, Inc. (NYSE: MLM) (Martin Marietta or the Company), a leading national supplier of aggregates and other building materials, today reported results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
[s6] 1Non-GAAP financial measures; see pages 14 and 16 for reconciliations to the nearest GAAP financial measures.

[s10] Ward Nye, Chair, President and CEO of Martin Marietta, stated, “Building on our positive trends entering 2026, Martin Marietta delivered record second-quarter revenues and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations.
[s11] Revenues increased 21% and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations grew 13%, driven by strong organic performance and acquisition contributions.
[s12] Based on our strong first-half results and continued momentum, we are raising our full-year revenue guidance to a range of $7.2 billion to $7.4 billion and reaffirming our full-year Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations guidance of $2.36 billion to $2.5 billion.
[s13] Most significantly, and consistent with our strategic plan, on June 27, we entered into a definitive agreement to combine with Lhoist North America (LNA), the nation's leading producer of high-calcium lime, dolomitic lime and industrial mineral products.
[s14] The planned combination advances our SOAR 2030 objective to expand our differentiated upstream Specialties platform, broadens our participation across infrastructure, manufacturing and industrial end markets and leverages our core quarrying and mineral resource management expertise.
[s15] As the transaction has not yet closed, our revised 2026 guidance does not include any contribution from LNA.
[s16] "Additionally, on May 15 we completed the acquisition of New Frontier Materials (NFM), expanding our leading aggregates platform along the I-70 corridor.
[s17] "Beyond these portfolio actions, our expanded enterprise review identified opportunities that are expected to generate approximately $350 million of annualized cash flow improvements as we optimize our evolving asset base, network footprint, and sustaining capital requirements.
[s18] Through disciplined inventory management and reductions in capital spending, we have unlocked more than $200 million of cash year-to-date compared with the prior-year period.
[s19] As we advance our SOAR 2030 objectives, we remain focused on responsible capital allocation, enterprise excellence and preserving the financial flexibility that has long distinguished our Company.
[s20] Second-quarter aggregates shipments increased 17.0 percent to a record of 61.6 million tons, reflecting a full quarter of contributions from the operations acquired from Quikrete Holdings, Inc. (QUIKRETE), a partial-quarter of contributions from NFM and organic shipment growth of 2.3 percent driven by strong infrastructure and heavy nonresidential demand across our geographic footprint.
[s21] ASP decreased 2.0 percent to $22.74 per ton, primarily reflecting acquisition-related mix headwinds.
[s22] Organic ASP increased 2.1 percent and organic mix-adjusted ASP7 increased 3.7 percent, reflecting continued strong organic shipment momentum in the Central and West Divisions where average selling prices are below the Company's average.
[s23] Aggregates gross profit decreased 3 percent to $418 million, inclusive of the $52 million non-cash charge associated with the fair market value purchase accounting inventory step-up adjustments.
[s24] Cost management efforts supported strong organic cost performance with cost of goods sold per ton increasing 3.6 percent, including 150 basis points from higher pass-through external freight costs.
[s25] Other Building Materials revenues increased 12 percent to $303 million while gross profit decreased 14 percent to $34 million.
[s26] Specialties delivered revenues of $152 million and gross profit of $50 million, both quarterly records.
[s27] These results reflected contributions from the July 2025 Premier Magnesia, LLC acquisition and organic pricing gains across all products.
[s28] The Company's lime business delivered 4.0 percent ASP growth, or 5.0 percent on a mix-adjusted8 basis, and 0.9 percent shipment growth resulting in gross profit growth of 7 percent.
[s29] On June 27, 2026, the Company entered into a definitive agreement to combine with LNA, a subsidiary of Lhoist Group, in a transaction valued at approximately $13.5 billion, consisting of cash and shares of Martin Marietta common stock.
[s30] The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
[s31] LNA is a leading producer of high-calcium lime, dolomitic lime and industrial mineral products serving diversified end markets through a network of 20 quarries and production facilities and 45 distribution terminals.
[s32] On May 15, 2026, the Company acquired NFM, a complementary aggregates-led bolt-on business serving the greater St. Louis metropolitan area producing over 8 million tons of aggregates annually.
[s33] Cash provided by operating activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026, was $339 million, compared with $605 million for the prior-year period, primarily reflecting higher income tax payments related to the taxable gain recognized on the February 2026 divestiture of the Midlothian cement business and the Company's remaining Texas ready mix concrete operations in conjunction with the QUIKRETE asset exchange completed February 2026.
[s34] Cash paid for property, plant and equipment additions for the six months ended June 30, 2026, was $314 million.
[s35] During the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company returned $302 million to shareholders through dividend payments and share repurchases.
[s36] As of June 30, 2026, 10.7 million shares remained available under the current repurchase authorization.
[s37] As of June 30, 2026, the Company had $112 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents on hand and $742 million of unused borrowing capacity under its existing credit facilities.
[s38] On July 15, 2026, the Company secured a commitment for a new three-year senior unsecured term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of $1.5 billion subject to consummation of the LNA acquisition and other customary conditions.

NXP Semiconductors delivered a stronger third quarter, with revenue climbing to **$3.79 billion**, up **19%** year-on-year and **8%** sequentially.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Revenue rose to **$3.79 billion**, growing **19%** from a year earlier.
- Sequential momentum also improved, with the top line advancing from the prior quarter.

**Profitability**
- GAAP gross margin was **57.8%**, while non-GAAP gross margin reached **58.6%**.

- Non-GAAP free cash flow was **$1.21 billion**, representing **31.9%** of revenue.

- The board authorized a **$5 billion** share repurchase program in October after quarter end, in addition to the **$1.3 billion** remaining under the prior authorization.

[s1] PACKAGING CORPORATION OF AMERICA REPORTS SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
[s2] Lake Forest, IL, July 22, 2026 – Packaging Corporation of America (NYSE: PKG) today reported second quarter 2026 net income of $192 million, or $2.15 per share, and net income of $210 million, or $2.35 per share, excluding special items.
[s3] Second quarter net sales were $2.5 billion in 2026 and $2.2 billion in 2025.
[s4] Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2026 include special items primarily for facility closure costs and write-offs, costs related to the restructuring of the Wallula, WA containerboard mill and acquisition and integration-related costs.
[s5] Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2025 included special items relating to gains on the sale of real estate in connection with the closure of corrugated products facilities, partially offset by acquisition and integration related costs.
[s6] Excluding special items, the ($.13) per share decrease in second quarter 2026 earnings compared to the second quarter of 2025 resulted from ($.27) lower earnings in the legacy business, partially offset by $.14 of earnings from the acquired Greif operations.
[s7] The lower earnings in the legacy business was driven by higher freight costs ($0.26), higher corporate and other expenses ($.12), unfavorable price and mix in the packaging business ($.11), higher labor and operating costs ($.05), higher depreciation and amortization expenses ($.03), higher fiber costs ($.02), higher tax rate ($.02) and higher interest expense, excluding Greif acquisition indebtedness ($.01).
[s8] These items were partially offset by higher production and sales volume in the packaging business $.26, lower maintenance outage expenses $.04, higher production and sales volume in the paper business $.03 and higher price and mix in the paper business $.02.
[s9] The $.14 of Greif earnings during the quarter included a $0.04 benefit to depreciation expense due to measurement period adjustments for the valuation of certain fixed assets on the opening balance sheet of the acquired business.
[s10] Earnings were $.02 above second quarter guidance of $2.33 per share primarily due to favorable volume in the legacy packaging business, lower production costs in the legacy packaging business and higher than expected earnings from the acquired business due to favorable volume, price and mix, partially offset by higher-than-forecast costs for freight, recycled fiber and employee benefits.
[s11] Total corrugated products shipments were up 24.3% per day and in total compared to the second quarter of 2025.
[s12] In the legacy packaging business, corrugated products shipments were up 4.1% per day and in total compared to the second quarter of 2025, with the same number of shipping days in each period.
[s13] Containerboard production was 1,415,000 tons, and containerboard inventory was down 25,000 tons compared to the first quarter of 2026 and up 40,000 tons compared to the second quarter of 2025, primarily due to the acquisition.
[s14] In the Paper segment, sales volume was up 6.3% from the second quarter of 2025.
[s15] We continued to operate our mill system at full capacity and reduced export sales by approximately 30,000 tons from first quarter levels to support our corrugated products demand.
[s16] Considering these items, we expect third quarter earnings of $ 2.91 per share, excluding special items.”
[s17] PCA operates ten mills and 90 corrugated products plants and related facilities.

# Philip Morris International Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

Philip Morris International delivered higher revenue and operating income in the third quarter, with adjusted earnings reaching a new quarterly high despite a decline in reported earnings per share.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Revenue climbed **5.5%** to **$11.4 billion**, or **7.1%** on an organic basis.
- Gross profit rose **6.7%**, helped by combustible pricing, scale and smoke-free mix benefits.

**Profitability**
- Operating income jumped **14.1%**.
- Reported diluted EPS slipped **4.9%** to **$2.12**, mainly due to the non-cash fair value adjustment for equity security investments.
- Adjusted diluted EPS grew **5.4%** to **$2.36**, and by **5.8%** excluding currency.

**Product Performance**
- Total shipments edged up **0.6%**, while smoke-free product shipments rose **2.7%**.
- IQOS heated tobacco unit shipment volumes grew **1.5%** to **41.5 billion** units.
- VEEV quarterly shipments surged **61.6%**.
- In the U.S., total ZYN shipments increased **4.2%** to **3.2 billion** pouches.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- The regular quarterly dividend was increased **8.8%** to **$1.60** per share.
- Full-year operating cash flow is expected to be around **$13.5 billion** at prevailing exchange rates.

**Outlook**
- Reported diluted EPS is forecast in a range of **$7.11** to **$7.26** for the full year.
- Net revenue growth is expected at **5%** to **7%** on an organic basis, with a greater likelihood to be in the middle or upper-half of the range.

**Bottom Line**
The quarter showed resilient underlying growth led by smoke-free products, stronger operating performance and a higher dividend, even as reported EPS was weighed down by a non-cash adjustment.

[s1] Philip Morris International Reports 2026 Third-Quarter & First Nine-Months Results
[s2] and Updates 2026 Full-Year Adjusted Diluted EPS Forecast for Currency Only;
[s3] Third-Quarter Reported Diluted EPS declined by 4.9% to $2.12;
[s4] Adjusted Diluted EPS grew by 5.4% to $2.36; and by 5.8% excluding currency;
[s5] STAMFORD, CT, October 21, 2026 – Philip Morris International Inc. (PMI) (NYSE: PM) today announces its 2026 third-quarter results.1
[s6] Shipments increased by 0.6% in the quarter, driven by a 2.7% increase in smoke-free products (SFP), with shipment growth across all categories, supported by high single-digit growth in SFP adjusted in-market sales (IMS), which is the closest proxy to consumer offtake.
[s7] Net revenues increased by 5.5% (7.1% organically) to $11.4 billion, with growth across both smoke-free (up by 4.1%, 6.3% organically) and combustibles (up by 6.4%, 7.7% organically).
[s8] Our smoke-free business accounted for more than 40% of total net revenues in the third quarter, and around 42% on a year-to-date basis, with more than 30 markets above 50%.
[s9] PMI smoke-free products are now available in 110 markets.
[s10] Gross profit increased by 6.7% (8.3% organically), expanding gross margins through strong combustible pricing, scale and SFP mix benefits.
[s11] Operating income increased by 14.1% (10.5% organically), reflecting the underlying strength of the business.
[s12] Reported diluted EPS of $2.12 declined by 4.9%, mainly due to the non-cash fair value adjustment for equity security investments.
[s13] Adjusted diluted EPS grew by 5.4%, or by 5.8% excluding a one cent unfavorable currency impact to reach $2.36, another quarterly all-time high.
[s14] Net revenue growth of 0.7% (3.4% organically) was driven by 2.7% volume growth, against the backdrop of a challenging HTU comparison due to the phasing of shipments between periods, notably in Japan.
[s15] Strong adjusted IMS momentum continued, with an acceleration to 8.0% growth.
[s16] Gross profit grew by 0.8% (3.3% organically).
[s17] 1 Explanation of PMI's use of non-GAAP measures cited in this document and reconciliations to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measures can be found in the “Non-GAAP Measures, Glossary and Explanatory Notes” section of this release, in Exhibit 99.2 to the company's Form 8-K dated October 21, 2026, and here.
[s18] IQOS HTUs gained 1.0pp to reach 9.9% of combined cigarette and HTU industry volumes in markets where present and grew shipment volumes by 1.5% to 41.5 billion units, at the high end of our previously disclosed expectations.
[s19] HTU adjusted IMS grew by 7.1%.
[s20] Excluding Japan and Poland, adjusted IMS continued to grow in the double digits, increasing by 10%, reflecting broad-based growth across a variety of markets, underscoring the increasing geographic diversification of IQOS.
[s21] In Japan, PMI HTU adjusted IMS grew by 3.4%, or by 1.3% excluding the estimated consumer pantry-loading impact ahead of the October 1 excise-driven price increase (JPY20 per pack). This continues to be broadly in line with our expectations as consumers adjust following the first excise-driven price increase (JPY40 per pack) on April 1. IQOS maintained a strong category share at 68%, with SENTIA continuing to play a key role in capturing price-sensitive TEREA consumers.
[s22] In Europe, IQOS HTU adjusted IMS growth strengthened to an estimated 6.0%, notwithstanding ongoing disruptions in Ukraine and the continued impact of the characterizing flavor ban in Poland. IQOS HTU adjusted market share increased by 0.9pp to 11.6%. This growth was led by strong performance in many markets, notably Germany, Greece, Spain and Romania. Adjusted IMS in Italy continued its strong growth trajectory, underscoring the category's significant potential across the region. Excluding Poland, adjusted IMS volumes grew by around 8%.
[s23] Outside Europe and Japan, adjusted IMS grew by 12.7% and offtake share increased in key cities across the globe, including Riyadh, Kuala Lumpur, Mexico City, Jakarta and Taipei, underlining the global growth potential of the heat-not-burn category.
[s24] Oral SFP: Total oral SFP volumes turned positive, increasing by 0.5%, as growth in modern oral of 20.6% to 0.5 billion pouches more than offset declines in the legacy Nordic snus business.
[s25] We continue to expand ZYN's footprint, with ZYN now available in 62 international markets and showing promising growth in geographies such as Global Travel Retail, Poland, and the Philippines, as well as sequential improvements in Sweden.
[s26] E-vapor SFP: We continue to drive outstanding growth in VEEV, with quarterly shipments up by 61.6%.
[s27] Net revenues grew by 6.5% (7.8% organically), driven by another impressive quarter of 8.9% pricing, partly offset by geographic mix.
[s28] Gross profit grew by 8.6% (9.8% organically).
[s29] Our cigarette category volume share stood at 25.9% (up by 0.4pp) despite adverse market mix.
[s30] Marlboro continued to gain share (up by 0.5pp) reaching a record category share of 11.4%.
[s31] In the U.S., total ZYN shipments grew by 4.2% to 3.2 billion pouches, despite challenging comparisons against a special promotional campaign last year and supported by the ongoing launches of ZYN ULTRA, new flagship dry flavors, 1.5mg and 8mg flagship variants.
[s32] Segment net revenues grew by 22.7% and gross profit by 24.2% (23.8% organically), driven by volume growth combined with favorable pricing comparisons due to prior year promotional activities.
[s33] Operating companies income decreased by 3.3% (increased by 1.5% organically), including a significant increase in commercial investments to support the expansion of our ZYN portfolio, which increased its category share by over 100 basis points between June and September, as estimated by Nielsen.
[s34] This reflects a ramp-up in consumer communications, notably an expansion of the 'When It Clicks' brand campaign, and the transition of the majority of the ZYN flagship portfolio to 20-pouch cans (from 15-pouch cans today), including associated transitional support programs.
[s35] The change to 20-pouch cans is designed to align the value proposition across the portfolio and optimize ZYN's price premium to support future growth in the dynamic U.S. nicotine pouch category.
[s36] On August 21, the FDA granted PMTA authorization to 11 variants of ZYN ULTRA, our higher-nicotine moist offering.
[s37] ZYN now has PMTA authorization of 31 variants in total, more than any other nicotine brand on the market.
[s38] This, combined with the MRTP authorization of 20 ZYN flagship variants on June 30, underlines the robustness of the science behind our products and their potential to reduce the harm caused by smoking.
[s39] Dividend: Increased regular quarterly dividend by 8.8% to $1.60 per share, or an annualized $6.40 per share.
[s40] Reported diluted EPS is forecast to be in a range of $7.11 to $7.26, at prevailing exchange rates.
[s41] Excluding a total 2026 adjustment of $1.18 per share, this forecast represents a projected increase of 9.9% to 11.9% versus adjusted diluted EPS of $7.54 in 2025.
[s42] This includes a favorable currency impact of $0.18, at prevailing exchange rates (previously $0.24).
[s43] Excluding currency, this forecast represents a projected increase of 7.5% to 9.5% versus adjusted diluted EPS of $7.54 in 2025, as outlined in the above table.
[s44] 2026 Full-Year Forecast Assumptions
[s45] Growing (previously broadly stable to slightly growing) total PMI cigarette and SFP shipment volume, with high single-digit SFP shipment growth, led by high single-digit SFP adjusted IMS growth, and a cigarette shipment volume decline at a similar level to the year-to-date trend (previously around 2% to 3%);
[s46] Net revenue growth of 5% to 7% on an organic basis; with a greater likelihood to be in the middle or upper-half of the range, supported by a fourth-quarter reacceleration in international smoke-free;
[s47] Organic operating income growth of 7% to 9%; with a greater likelihood to be in the middle or lower-half of the range, with a corresponding flow through to our EPS forecast range, given the cost impacts of ongoing geopolitical tensions and the previously communicated step-up in U.S. growth investments;

[s1] ROLLINS, INC. REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS
[s2] ATLANTA, GEORGIA, October 21, 2026: Rollins, Inc. (NYSE:ROL) (“Rollins” or the “Company”), a premier global consumer and commercial services company, reported unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.
[s3] Third quarter revenues were $1.1 billion, an increase of 6.2% over the third quarter of 2025 with organic revenues* increasing 4.4% compared to the prior year.
[s4] Quarterly operating income was $223 million, a decrease of 1.0% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Quarterly operating margin was 20.5%, a decrease of 140 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted operating income* was $231 million, a decrease of 0.6% versus the prior year. Adjusted operating margin* was 21.2%, a decrease of 140 basis points compared to the prior year.
[s5] Quarterly net income was $158 million, a decrease of 3.4% compared to the prior year. Adjusted net income* was $163 million, a decrease of 3.1% versus the prior year.
[s6] Adjusted EBITDA* was $257 million, a decrease of 0.7% compared to the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA margin* was 23.5%, a decrease of 170 basis points versus the third quarter of 2025.
[s7] Quarterly EPS was $0.33 per diluted share, a 2.9% decrease compared to the prior year. Adjusted EPS* was $0.34 per diluted share, a decrease of 2.9% versus the prior year.
[s8] Operating cash flow was $242 million for the quarter, an increase of 26.4% compared to the prior year. Free cash flow* was $235 million for the quarter, an increase of 28.8% compared to the prior year. Cash flow was favorably impacted by $63 million due to the timing of a tax refund associated with our tax credit planning strategy. The Company invested $27 million in acquisitions, $6 million in capital expenditures, $120 million in share repurchases, and paid dividends totaling $87 million.
[s9] At the same time, our record of 100 consecutive quarters of revenue growth reflects the durability of our business and our ability to successfully adapt through changing conditions.

[s15] Through its family of leading brands, the Company and its franchises provide essential pest control services and protection against termite damage, rodents, and insects to more than 2.8 million customers in North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and Australia, with approximately 22,000 employees from more than 850 locations.

# Ross Stores Q2 FY2026 Earnings Summary

Ross Stores delivered a strong second quarter, with sales climbing **13%** to **$6.3 billion**, helped by robust customer traffic.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Comparable store sales jumped **10%** for the quarter.
- For the first six months of fiscal 2026, sales grew **17%** to **$12.3 billion**.
- Comparable store sales for the six-month period advanced **13%**.

**Profitability**
- Operating profits reached **$1.1 billion**, including approximately **$253 million** from IEEPA tariff refunds.
- Operating margin expanded **610 basis points**, including **405 basis points** from the tariff refunds.
- Net income rose to **$851 million**, while earnings per share climbed to **$2.66**.
- The results included an approximate **$0.60** per share benefit from the tariff refunds.

**Store Expansion and Capital Returns**
- The company opened **47** new stores during the quarter.
- A total of **1.4 million** shares were repurchased for an aggregate price of **$319 million**.
- The company remains on track to buy back a total of **$1.275 billion** in common stock during fiscal 2026.

**Outlook**
- Comparable store sales are expected to increase **6%** to **7%** in the third quarter and **4%** to **5%** in the fourth quarter.
- The new store opening plan for 2026 was increased to **115** locations.
- Fiscal year 2026 earnings per share are now projected to be in the range of **$8.61** to **$8.77**.

**Bottom Line**
The company posted broad-based sales and profit strength in the quarter, supported by tariff refunds, and raised its outlook for the second half and full fiscal year.

[s1] Raises Second Half and Fiscal 2026 Outlook
[s2] Dublin, California, August 20, 2026 -- Ross Stores, Inc. (Nasdaq: ROST) today reported financial results for the 13‑week quarter ended August 1, 2026.
(lead-in) Highlights:
[s3] Total sales for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 13% versus last year, with comparable store sales up a very strong 10%, primarily driven by customer traffic.
[s4] Second quarter operating profits were $1.1 billion, which includes approximately $253 million from IEEPA tariff refunds. Operating margin increased 610 basis points, including 405 basis points from the tariff refunds. Excluding this benefit, operating margin increased by 205 basis points, well above the Company’s plan for an increase of 130 to 150 basis points.
[s5] Earnings per share for the second quarter were $2.66, which includes an approximate $0.60 per share benefit from the tariff refunds, well above our guidance of $1.85 to $1.93.
[s6] Opened 47 new stores during the quarter, including 35 Ross and 12 dd’s DISCOUNTS. Increasing 2026 store opening plans to 115 new locations.
[s7] ROSS STORES, INC. 5130 Hacienda Drive, Dublin, CA 94568 (925) 965-4400
[s8] Sales for the second quarter increased 13% to $6.3 billion, up from $5.5 billion in 2025.
[s9] Comparable store sales rose a very strong 10% for the quarter on top of a 2% gain last year.
[s10] Net income was $851 million versus $508 million last year, while earnings per share were $2.66 compared to $1.56 per share in the prior year period.
[s11] For the first six months of fiscal 2026, sales increased a robust 17% to $12.3 billion, up from $10.5 billion in 2025.
[s12] Comparable store sales for the six-month period were up 13%.
[s13] Net income was $1.5 billion versus $987 million last year, while earnings per share were $4.69 compared to $3.03 per share in the prior year period.
[s14] Both the second quarter and first six months 2026 results include about $253 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, benefiting earnings per share by approximately $0.60.
[s15] During the 2026 second quarter, a total of 1.4 million shares of common stock were repurchased for an aggregate price of $319 million under the Company’s two-year $2.55 billion authorization approved by its Board of Directors in March 2026.
[s16] The Company remains on track to buy back a total of $1.275 billion in common stock during fiscal 2026.
[s17] Comparable store sales are now expected to increase 6% to 7% in the third quarter and 4% to 5% in the fourth quarter.
[s18] If the second half of 2026 performs in line with these sales projections, our earnings per share ranges for the third and fourth quarters are projected to be $1.75 to $1.83 and $2.17 to $2.26, respectively.”
[s19] Mr. Conroy continued, “Based on our strong first half results and our updated second half guidance, we are increasing our 2026 fiscal year earnings per share projections to be in the range of $8.61 to $8.77, which again includes an approximate $0.60 earnings per share benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds recognized in the second quarter.
[s20] As a result, we are increasing our 2026 new store opening plan to 115 locations, consisting of approximately 90 Ross Dress for Less and 25 dd’s DISCOUNTS stores.”
[s21] The Company will host a conference call on Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 4:15 p.m. Eastern time to provide additional details concerning its second quarter results and management’s outlook for the second half and fiscal year 2026.
[s22] An audio playback will be available at 201-612-7415, PIN #13762049 until 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on August 27, 2026, as well as on the Company’s website.
[s23] Other risk factors are set forth in our SEC filings including the Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 Form 8-Ks and 10-Q on file with the SEC.
[s24] Ross Stores, Inc. is an S&P 500, Fortune 500, and Nasdaq 100 (ROST) company headquartered in Dublin, California, with fiscal 2025 revenues of $22.8 billion.
[s25] Currently, the Company operates Ross Dress for Less® ("Ross"), the largest off-price apparel and home fashion chain in the United States with 1,952 locations in 44 states, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
[s26] Ross offers first-quality, in-season, brand name and designer apparel, accessories, footwear, and home fashions for the entire family at savings of 20% to 60% off department and specialty store regular prices every day.
[s27] The Company also operates 376 dd's DISCOUNTS® stores in 23 states that feature a more moderately-priced assortment of first-quality, in-season apparel, accessories, footwear, and home fashions for the entire family at savings of 20% to 70% off moderate department and discount store regular prices every day.

Starbucks Q3 Fiscal 2026: Comparable Sales Strength Offsets China-Related Revenue Decline
Transaction-led comparable sales growth lifted earnings sharply even as consolidated revenue eased after the China transaction.
Consolidated net revenues slipped 1% to $9.3 billion, reflecting the conversion of the China retail business to a licensed joint venture model. Global comparable store sales climbed 7.9%, driven by a 4.2% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket.
Profitability improved markedly. GAAP earnings per share rose 86% to $0.91, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 70% to $0.85. GAAP operating margin expanded to 10.5%, and non-GAAP operating margin widened to 14.4%, helped by sales leverage and lower inflation paired with tariff refunds.
By segment, North America net revenues grew 7% to $7.4 billion, with operating margin reaching 13.6%. International net revenues fell 34% to $1.3 billion following the China conversion, while Channel Development net revenues jumped 22% to $587.9 million on strength in the Global Coffee Alliance.
The company used a portion of the China sale proceeds to complete tender offers to purchase approximately $1.3 billion aggregate principal amount of certain outstanding notes. The Board also declared a cash dividend of $0.62 per share.
Outlook: For the fourth quarter, the company expects U.S. comparable store sales growth of 6.5% or greater, leading to full fiscal year 2026 U.S. comparable store sales growth of slightly greater than 6.0%. It also guided to non-GAAP consolidated operating margin greater than 11.0% and non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of $2.55 to $2.65.

[s1] Starbucks Reports Q3 Fiscal Year 2026 Results
[s2] Global Q3 Comparable Store Sales Up 7.9%, Led by Transaction Growth
[s3] Q3 Consolidated Net Revenues Down 1% to $9.3 billion, Reflecting the Starbucks China Transaction
[s4] Q3 GAAP EPS $0.91, Non-GAAP EPS $0.85
[s5] Raises Fiscal Year 2026 Guidance
[s6] SEATTLE; July 29, 2026 – Starbucks Corporation (Nasdaq: SBUX) today reported financial results for its 13-week fiscal third quarter ended June 28, 2026.
[s7] GAAP results in fiscal 2026 include items that are excluded from non-GAAP results.
[s8] Q3 Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights
[s9] Global comparable store sales increased 7.9%, primarily driven by a 4.2% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket
[s10] North America comparable store sales increased 8.1%, primarily driven by a 4.5% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket; U.S. comparable store sales increased 7.9%, primarily driven by a 4.2% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.6% increase in average ticket
[s11] International comparable store sales increased 5.7%, primarily driven by a 3.1% increase in average ticket and a 2.6% increase in comparable transactions
[s12] The company opened 175 net new stores in Q3, ending the period with 41,304 stores: 33% company-operated and 67% licensed
[s13] At the end of Q3, stores in the U.S. comprised 41% of the company’s global portfolio, ending the period with 16,933 stores
[s14] Consolidated net revenues decreased 1% to $9.3 billion, including on a constant currency basis
[s15] GAAP operating margin expanded 60 basis points year-over-year to 10.5%, primarily driven by sales leverage and lower inflation paired with tariff refunds, partially offset by higher restructuring costs and labor investments largely in support of “Back to Starbucks”
[s16] Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 430 basis points year-over-year to 14.4%, including on a constant currency basis
[s17] The company used a portion of the China sale proceeds to complete a series of tender offers to purchase approximately $1.3 billion aggregate principal amount of certain series of the company's outstanding notes
[s18] Effective tax rate of 26.4% compared to 31.8% in the prior year, with the decrease primarily due to lapping the discrete impact of changes in indefinite reinvestment assertions for certain foreign entities in the third quarter of fiscal 2025, partially offset by impacts resulting from the divestiture of Starbucks retail operations in China in the third quarter of fiscal 2026
[s19] Non-GAAP effective tax rate decreased 960 basis points to 21.8%
[s20] GAAP earnings per share of $0.91 increased 86% over prior year
[s21] Non-GAAP earnings per share of $0.85 expanded 70% over prior year, including on a constant currency basis
[s22] Q3 North America Segment Results
[s23] Net revenues for the North America segment increased 7% over Q3 FY25 to $7.4 billion in Q3 FY26, primarily driven by an increase in company-operated store revenue due to an 8.1% increase in comparable store sales, driven by a 4.5% increase in comparable transactions and a 3.5% increase in average ticket, primarily due to higher delivery sales and strength in customer food attach and beverage modifications.
[s24] Operating income increased to $1.0 billion in Q3 FY26 compared to $918.7 million in Q3 FY25.
[s25] Operating margin of 13.6% expanded from 13.3% in the prior year, primarily driven by sales leverage, lapping of the Leadership Experience 2025, and lower inflation paired with tariff refunds.
[s26] Q3 International Segment Results
[s27] Net revenues for the International segment decreased 34% over Q3 FY25 to $1.3 billion in Q3 FY26, primarily driven by the conversion of Starbucks retail operations in China to our licensed joint venture model in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 which drove lower company-operated store revenues and largely contributed to higher product sales to, and royalty revenue from, our licensees.
[s28] Operating income decreased to $252.8 million in Q3 FY26 compared to $272.7 million in Q3 FY25.
[s29] Operating margin of 19.1% expanded from 13.6% in the prior year, primarily driven by the conversion of Starbucks retail operations in China to our licensed joint venture model in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
[s30] Q3 Channel Development Segment Results
[s31] Net revenues for the Channel Development segment increased 22% over Q3 FY25 to $587.9 million in Q3 FY26, primarily due to an increase in revenue in the Global Coffee Alliance.
[s32] Operating income increased to $306.2 million in Q3 FY26 compared to $218.4 million in Q3 FY25.
[s33] Operating margin of 52.1% expanded from 45.1% in the prior year, primarily driven by tariff impacts including refunds.
[s34] 1.In April, Starbucks completed the previously announced transaction with funds managed by Boyu Capital to operate Starbucks retail business in China, marking an important milestone in the company's strategy to support sustainable, disciplined growth in the market.
[s35] Starbucks retains a 40% ownership interest in the joint venture and continues to own and license the Starbucks brand and intellectual property.
[s36] 2.Effective April 20, 2026, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection launched a platform for importers of record to begin submitting International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refund requests.
[s37] Starbucks submitted refund requests in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 for qualifying reciprocal tariffs paid and has received substantially all of the refunds requested, which were recorded in product and distribution costs within the consolidated statements of earnings.
[s38] The refunds received during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 largely offset related tariffs incurred in the first three quarters of fiscal 2026.
[s39] 3.In May, the company celebrated nearly 20,000 partners (employees) who graduated through the Starbucks College Achievement Plan to date, offering eligible partners 100 percent upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor's degree through Arizona State University's online degree program.
[s40] 4.In July, the company published its Global Impact Report, highlighting progress across coffee, partner opportunity, community impact, and environmental initiatives, while advancing several long-term goals and investments that help support the future of coffee, strengthen communities and create lasting positive impact.
[s41] 5.The Board declared a cash dividend of $0.62 per share, payable on August 28, 2026, to shareholders of record on August 14, 2026.
[s42] The company had 65 consecutive quarters of dividend payouts with CAGR of 17% over that time period, demonstrating the company's commitment to consistent value creation for shareholders.
[s43] Fiscal Year 2026 Guidance
[s44] The company updates its fiscal year 2026 guidance (all growth targets are relative to fiscal year 2025 non-GAAP measures unless specified):
[s45] Fourth quarter U.S. comparable store sales growth of 6.5% or greater, leading to:
[s46] Full fiscal year 2026 U.S. comparable store sales growth of slightly greater than 6.0%; and
[s47] Full fiscal year 2026 global comparable store sales growth nearing 6.0%.
[s48] Non-GAAP consolidated operating margin greater than 11.0%;
[s49] Non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of $2.55 to $2.65; and
[s50] Approximately 600 to 650 net new coffeehouses globally across company-operated and licensed businesses.
[s51] Guidance reflects the retail operations of Starbucks China as a joint venture licensee structure in the second half of the fiscal year 2026.
[s52] The retail operations of Starbucks China are reported as a company‑operated business for the first half of fiscal year 2026.
[s53] Starbucks will hold a conference call today at 1:15 p.m. Pacific Time, which will be hosted by Brian Niccol, chairman and ceo, and Cathy Smith, cfo.
[s54] A replay of the webcast will be available until end of day Friday, September 11, 2026.
[s55] Since 1971, Starbucks Coffee Company has been committed to responsibly sourcing and roasting high-quality arabica coffee.

# The J.M. Smucker Company Q1 FY2027 Earnings Summary

The J.M. Smucker Company opened fiscal 2027 with net sales of **$2.2 billion**, up **5%** from the prior year, aided by higher coffee pricing and tariff refunds received during the quarter.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Net sales rose by **$106.0 million**, with net price realization adding **4 percentage points** to growth, primarily driven by higher net pricing for coffee.
- Volume/mix contributed **1 percentage point**, helped by gains for Uncrustables® sandwiches and coffee, partly offset by declines for sweet baked goods and peanut butter.

**Profitability**
- Net income per diluted share was **$3.03**, while adjusted earnings per share climbed **71%** to **$3.24**, including an **$0.84** benefit from tariff refunds.
- Gross profit jumped by **$504.9 million**, or **106%**, reflecting tariff refunds received during the quarter.

**Segment Performance**
- One segment posted a **$90.6 million**, or **13%**, increase in net sales, while segment profit surged by **$165.8 million** on tariff refunds and higher net price realization, partly offset by higher marketing spend; volume/mix gains were led by the Dunkin’® and Café Bustelo® brands.
- Another segment saw net sales slip by **$16.7 million**, or **7%**, as weaker volume/mix for snack cakes and breakfast weighed on results.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- Cash provided by operating activities reached **$425.7 million**, a sharp improvement from cash used in the prior year.
- Free cash flow was **$337.3 million**, also swinging higher versus the prior year on the stronger operating cash flow.

**Outlook**
- For full-year fiscal 2027, the company now expects net sales to decrease **1.0%** to **2.0%** versus the prior year.
- Adjusted earnings per share is expected to range from **$10.50** to **$11.00**, with free cash flow of approximately **$1.1 billion**.

**Bottom Line**
The quarter combined pricing-led sales growth, a substantial tariff-refund benefit and much stronger cash generation, even as the updated full-year outlook points to softer sales ahead.

# UnitedHealth Group Q3 2025 Earnings Summary
UnitedHealth Group reported third-quarter 2025 results and raised its full-year 2025 earnings outlook, reflecting continued execution on its performance agenda and a refocus on its mission and culture.

**Revenue and Growth**
- Consolidated revenues climbed to **$113.2 billion**, up **12%** year-over-year.

**Profitability**
- GAAP earnings were **$2.59** per share, while adjusted earnings reached **$2.92** per share.
- Earnings from operations totaled **$4.3 billion**, with a net margin of **2.1%**.
- The medical care ratio came in at **89.9%**, in line with expectations outlined in the second quarter 2025.
- The operating cost ratio was **13.5%**, reflecting investments to support future growth.

**Segment Performance**
- UnitedHealthcare revenues grew **16%** year-over-year to **$87.1 billion**, driven by growth in Medicare & Retirement and Community & State.
- UnitedHealthcare served **50.1 million** consumers domestically, up **795,000** year-over-year.
- Optum revenues rose **8%** year-over-year to **$69.2 billion**, driven by growth in Optum Rx.
- Medicare & Retirement revenues surged to **$43.4 billion**, up **24%** year-over-year, while Community & State revenues climbed **18%** to **$23.8 billion**.

**Cash Flow and Balance Sheet**
- Cash flows from operations were **$5.9 billion**, or **2.3x** net income.
- The debt-to-capital ratio at September 30, 2025 was **44.1%**, unchanged from the second quarter 2025.

**Outlook**
- The company raised its full-year 2025 outlook to net earnings of at least **$14.90** per share and adjusted net earnings of at least **$16.25** per share.

**Bottom Line**
The quarter showed solid revenue growth across the company's businesses and an increased full-year earnings outlook, even as elevated medical cost trends continued to pressure profitability.

[s7] (October 28, 2025) UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) reported third quarter 2025 results, reflecting the continued execution on its performance agenda, refocus on its mission and culture, and return to sustained growth.
[s8] “We remain focused on strengthening performance and positioning for durable and accelerating growth in 2026 and beyond, and our results this quarter reflect solid execution toward that goal,” said Stephen Hemsley, chief executive officer of UnitedHealth Group.
[s9] UnitedHealth Group raised its 2025 earnings outlook to reflect net earnings of at least $14.90 per share and adjusted net earnings of at least $16.25 per share.
[s10] Third Quarter 2025 Key Performance Metrics
[s11] Consolidated revenues of $113.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year.
[s12] Earnings from operations were $4.3 billion; net margin of 2.1%.
[s13] Adjusted EPS of $2.92; GAAP EPS of $2.59.
[s14] Medical care ratio (MCR) of 89.9% was in line with expectations outlined in the second quarter 2025.
[s15] Operating cost ratio of 13.5% reflecting investments to support future growth.
[s16] UnitedHealthcare revenues grew 16% year-over-year to $87.1 billion, driven by growth in Medicare & Retirement and Community & State; UnitedHealthcare served 50.1 million consumers domestically, up 795,000 year-over-year.
[s17] Optum revenues grew 8% year-over-year to $69.2 billion, driven by growth in Optum Rx.
[s18] September 30, 2025, debt-to-capital ratio of 44.1% unchanged from the second quarter 2025 and inclusive of the impact of closing the Amedisys transaction on August 14, 2025.
[s19] UnitedHealth Group’s third quarter 2025 revenues grew $12.3 billion year-over-year to $113.2 billion.
[s20] Third quarter earnings from operations were $4.3 billion and adjusted net earnings were $2.92 per share.
[s21] The third quarter consolidated medical care ratio of 89.9% reflected utilization in line with expectations outlined in the second quarter 2025. The year-over-year increase of 470 basis points was primarily driven by the previously described significantly elevated cost trends, as well as the ongoing effects of the Biden-era Medicare funding reductions and changes to the Part D program from the Inflation Reduction Act. Medical reserve development was $80 million favorable in the third quarter 2025.
[s22] Days claims payable of 46.2 compared to 44.5 in the second quarter 2025 and 47.4 in third quarter 2024. Days sales outstanding were flat year-over-year at 18.6 and down 1.3 days sequentially.
[s23] The third quarter 2025 operating cost ratio of 13.5% compared to 13.2% in the year ago quarter.
[s24] Cash flows from operations were $5.9 billion in the third quarter 2025, or 2.3x net income.
[s25] UnitedHealthcare’s third quarter 2025 revenues of $87.1 billion grew $12.2 billion or 16% year-over-year. UnitedHealthcare served 50.1 million people domestically in the third quarter 2025, an increase of 795,000 year-over-year.
[s26] UnitedHealthcare’s third quarter 2025 earnings from operations were $1.8 billion compared to $4.2 billion in third quarter 2024. Third quarter 2025 operating margin of 2.1% compared to 5.6% in third quarter 2024, primarily due to elevated medical cost trend, the effects of the Biden-era Medicare funding reductions and Part D IRA impacts.
[s27] UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual third quarter 2025 revenues were $19.9 billion compared to $19.8 billion in third quarter 2024.
[s28] The number of people served domestically increased by 200,000 year-over-year, with growth in employer self-funded offerings of 660,000 partially offset by attrition in both group fully-insured and individual products.
[s29] UnitedHealthcare Medicare & Retirement third quarter 2025 revenues of $43.4 billion grew $8.5 billion or 24% year-over-year due to growth in the number of people served and the effects of the Part D IRA impacts.
[s30] People served with individual and group Medicare Advantage offerings grew 85,000 in the third quarter 2025 and 625,000 year-over-year.
[s31] UnitedHealthcare Community & State third quarter 2025 revenues of $23.8 billion grew 18% year-over-year, driven by growth in serving people with complex needs and Medicaid rate improvements.
[s32] Members served contracted by 30,000 in the third quarter 2025.
[s33] Optum Health’s third quarter 2025 revenues of $25.9 billion were flat year-over-year.
[s34] Third quarter 2025 earnings from operations were $255 million, reflecting an operating margin of 1%. This compares to operating earnings of $2.2 billion and an operating margin of 8.3% in the third quarter 2024. The year-over-year decline was driven by continued reimbursement pressure due to the Medicare funding reductions and elevated utilization and costs.
[s35] Optum Insight’s third quarter 2025 revenues of $4.9 billion were flat year-over-year.
[s36] Third quarter 2025 earnings from operations were $706 million compared to $791 million a year ago and operating margins were 14.4% and 16.0%, respectively, due to investments to support future growth. The contract revenue backlog was $32.1 billion.
[s37] Optum Rx’s third quarter 2025 revenues of $39.7 billion increased 16% year-over-year driven by growth in script volumes from new clients and growth in existing clients, as well as growth in pharmacy services.
[s38] Earnings from operations for third quarter 2025 were $1.5 billion compared to $1.5 billion a year ago and operating margins were 3.9% and 4.5%, respectively. The operating margin decline year-over-year was primarily due to the mix effects of higher cost drugs driving higher revenue growth in the third quarter 2025 but with lower margins. Adjusted scripts grew to 414 million, up from 407 million last year.

Vici Properties Q3 2026: AFFO Growth Despite CECL Hit
Vici Properties delivered higher AFFO per share in the third quarter as revenue climbed, even as a CECL allowance change weighed heavily on reported earnings.
Total revenues reached $1.1 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. The result included $132.0 million of non-cash leasing and financing adjustments and $19.0 million of other income, pointing to continued flow-through from the portfolio.
Net income attributable to common stockholders slipped 55.1% to $342.5 million, or $0.31 per share, with the decline driven by the $478.2 million aggregate change in the CECL allowance. AFFO attributable to common stockholders fared better, growing 7.5% to $685.2 million, while AFFO per share rose 4.3% to $0.62.
On capital, the company issued $1.75 billion of investment grade senior notes at an adjusted weighted average interest rate of 5.422% to refinance 2026 maturities. It ended the quarter with $270.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, approximately $17.2 billion in total debt and approximately $2.5 billion in liquidity. The quarterly cash dividend was declared at $0.46 per share, up 2.2% year-over-year, and, subsequent to quarter-end, the board authorized a share repurchase program for up to $2.0 billion.
