[s1] VICI PROPERTIES INC. ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
[s2] - Completed $1.75 Billion Investment Grade Senior Notes Offering -
[s3] - Increased Annual Dividend for 9th Consecutive Year -
[s4] - Raised Guidance for Full Year 2026 -
[s5] NEW YORK, NY – October 28, 2026 – VICI Properties Inc. (NYSE: VICI) (“VICI Properties”, “VICI” or the “Company”), an experiential real estate investment trust, today reported results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
[s6] Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights
[s7] Total revenues increased 5.8% year-over-year to $1.1 billion
[s8] Net income attributable to common stockholders decreased 55.1% year-over-year to $342.5 million and, on a per share basis, decreased 56.4% year-over-year to $0.31 due to the impact of the change in the CECL allowance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026
[s9] AFFO attributable to common stockholders increased 7.5% year-over-year to $685.2 million and, on a per share basis, increased 4.3% year-over-year to $0.62
[s10] Declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.46 per share, representing a 2.2% year-over-year increase
[s11] Issued $1.75 billion of investment grade senior notes to refinance 2026 maturities
[s12] Ended the quarter with $270.3 million in cash and cash equivalents
[s13] Raised AFFO guidance for full year 2026 to between $2,695 million and $2,705 million, or between $2.47 and $2.48 per diluted share
[s14] Subsequent to quarter-end, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for up to $2.0 billion in shares
[s15] Edward Pitoniak, Chief Executive Officer of VICI Properties, said, “In the third quarter of 2026, we grew our quarterly revenue by 5.8% and our AFFO per share by 4.3% year-over-year, once again demonstrating the flow-through efficiency of our business model, and we were pleased to announce our 9th consecutive annual dividend increase since our IPO almost nine years ago.
[s16] Our commitment to situational readiness positioned us to refinance all of our remaining 2026 maturities through a $1.75 billion investment grade notes offering in August at an adjusted weighted average interest rate of 5.42%.
[s17] Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
[s18] Total revenues were $1.1 billion for the quarter, an increase of 5.8% compared to $1.0 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s19] Total revenues for the quarter included $132.0 million of non-cash leasing and financing adjustments and $19.0 million of other income.
[s20] Net income attributable to common stockholders was $342.5 million for the quarter, or $0.31 per share, compared to $762.0 million, or $0.71 per share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s21] The year-over-year decrease in net income was driven, on an absolute basis, by the $478.2 million aggregate change in the CECL allowance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s22] FFO attributable to common stockholders was $342.5 million for the quarter, or $0.31 per share, compared to $762.0 million, or $0.71 per share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s23] The year-over-year decrease in FFO was driven, on an absolute basis, by the $478.2 million aggregate change in the CECL allowance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s24] AFFO attributable to common stockholders was $685.2 million for the quarter, an increase of 7.5% compared to $637.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s25] AFFO per share was $0.62 for the quarter, an increase of 4.3% compared to $0.60 for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
[s26] Third Quarter 2026 Investment and Portfolio Activity
[s27] On September 28, 2026, VICI announced, in connection with Century Casinos, Inc.’s (NASDAQ: CNTY) (“Century Casinos”) agreement to sell the operations of Century Mile Racetrack and Century Downs Racetrack (together, the “Century Canada Racinos”), located in Alberta, Canada, to a subsidiary of Highfield Investment Group, Inc. (“Highfield”), its agreement to enter into a new separate triple-net master lease with a subsidiary of Highfield with respect to the real property of the Century Canada Racinos (the “Highfield Master Lease”) and to amend the Master Lease between VICI and Century Casinos (the “Century Master Lease”).
[s28] The Highfield Master Lease will have an initial annual base rent of C$10.7 million (approximately US$7.5 million as of the day prior to the announcement) and, if closing occurs after January 1, 2027, such base rent shall escalate as provided for in the Century Master Lease on such date.
[s29] Upon closing, the Highfield Master Lease will begin a new 20-year initial lease term with four 5-year tenant renewal options.
[s30] The other economic terms of the Highfield Master Lease will be substantially similar to the terms for the Century Canada Racinos under the Century Master Lease, including escalation equal to the greater of 1.25% and the change in Canadian CPI (capped at 2.50%) and a minimum capital expenditure requirement equal to 1.0% of annual net revenue at each property.
[s31] Upon closing, the Century Master Lease will be amended to account for Century Casinos' divestiture of the operations of the Century Canada Racinos, which will result in a corresponding reduction of the annual base rent under the Century Master Lease by C$10.7 million (approximately US$7.5 million as of the day prior to the announcement) with adjustments to reflect the escalated rent if the transaction closing occurs after January 1, 2027.
[s32] The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027.
[s33] Third Quarter 2026 and Subsequent Capital Markets Activity
[s34] On August 5, 2026, VICI priced the offering of $1.75 billion aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes (the “August 2026 Notes”).
[s35] On August 14, 2026, VICI issued the August 2026 Notes comprised of (i) $900.0 million aggregate principal amount of 5.400% Senior Notes due 2031, which mature on October 15, 2031, and (ii) $850.0 million aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Notes due 2036, which mature on October 15, 2036.
[s36] The weighted average interest rate for the August 2026 Notes is 5.570%, and the adjusted weighted average interest rate, after taking into account the impact of forward-starting interest rate swaps and treasury locks, is 5.422%.
[s37] The net proceeds of the August 2026 Notes were used to redeem the then-outstanding (i) $480.5 million aggregate principal amount of 4.500% Exchange Notes due 2026, (ii) $1,250.0 million aggregate principal amount of 4.250% November 2019 Notes due 2026, and (iii) $19.5 million aggregate principal amount of 4.500% MGP OP Notes due 2026.
[s38] During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, VICI entered into a combination of forward-starting interest rate swap agreements and treasury locks with an aggregate notional amount of $1.1 billion.
[s39] In connection with the August 2026 Notes offering, VICI settled the outstanding forward-starting interest rate swaps and treasury locks for total proceeds of $20.0 million.
[s40] Since the forward-starting swaps and treasury locks were hedging the interest rate risk on the anticipated issuance of the August 2026 Notes, the unrealized gain, which was recorded in Accumulated other comprehensive income on VICI's consolidated balance sheets, will be amortized over the term of the respective derivative instruments as a reduction in interest expense.
[s41] Subsequent to quarter-end, on October 27, 2026, VICI’s Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for up to $2.0 billion in shares of the Company’s common stock, which will expire on September 30, 2029.
[s42] Repurchases under the share repurchase program may be made from time to time at management’s discretion through open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions, Rule 10b5-1 plans or other methods, in each case in accordance with applicable securities laws.
[s43] As of September 30, 2026, the Company had approximately $17.2 billion in total debt and approximately $2.5 billion in liquidity, comprised of $270.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and approximately $2.2 billion of availability under its revolving credit facility.
[s44] The Company’s outstanding indebtedness as of September 30, 2026 was as follows:
[s45] (1) Based on applicable exchange rates as of September 30, 2026.
[s46] On September 3, 2026, the Company declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.46 per share, representing a 2.2% year-over-year increase.
[s47] The Q3 2026 dividend was paid on October 8, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 17, 2026 and totaled in aggregate approximately $506.3 million.
[s48] The Company is raising its AFFO guidance for the full year 2026.
[s49] In reliance on the exception provided by applicable rules, the Company does not provide guidance for GAAP net income, the most comparable GAAP financial measure, or a reconciliation of 2026 AFFO to GAAP net income because we are unable to predict with reasonable certainty the amount of the change in non-cash allowance for credit losses under ASU No. 2016-13 - Financial Instruments—Credit Losses (Topic 326) (“ASC 326”) for a future period.
[s50] The non-cash change in allowance for credit losses under ASC 326 with respect to a future period is dependent upon future events that are entirely outside of the Company’s control and may not be reliably predicted, including its tenants’ respective financial performance, fluctuations in the trading price of their common stock, credit ratings and outlook (each to the extent applicable), as well as broader macroeconomic performance.
[s51] The Company estimates AFFO for the year ending December 31, 2026 will be between $2,695 million and $2,705 million, or between $2.47 and $2.48 per diluted common share.
[s52] The following is a summary of the Company’s raised full-year 2026 guidance:
[s53] The Company will host a conference call and audio webcast on Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (ET).
[s54] Listeners who wish to participate in the question and answer session may do so via telephone by pre-registering on the Company’s earnings call registration webpage (https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BI4ddda18555004fa48ace389ea769214e).
[s55] VICI Properties Inc. is an S&P 500® experiential real estate investment trust that owns one of the largest portfolios of market-leading gaming, hospitality, wellness, entertainment and leisure destinations, including Caesars Palace Las Vegas, MGM Grand and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas, three of the most iconic entertainment facilities on the Las Vegas Strip.
[s56] VICI Properties owns 103 experiential assets across a geographically diverse portfolio consisting of 63 gaming properties and 40 other experiential properties across the United States and Canada.
[s57] The portfolio is comprised of approximately 130 million square feet and features approximately 66,000 hotel rooms and over 700 restaurants, bars, nightclubs and sportsbooks.
[s58] VICI Properties also owns four championship golf courses and approximately 33 acres of undeveloped and underdeveloped land adjacent to the Las Vegas Strip.

Veralto earnings rise in third quarter as company raises full-year outlook

Veralto reported third-quarter sales that climbed 7.5% to $1,509 million, with non-GAAP core sales growth of 5.1%.

Operating profit margin was 19.7%, while non-GAAP adjusted operating profit margin reached 25.6%. Net earnings were $253 million, or $1.03 per diluted common share, and non-GAAP adjusted net earnings were $290 million, or $1.18 per diluted common share.

[s1] Veralto Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
[s2] WALTHAM, Mass., (October 29, 2026) – Veralto (NYSE: VLTO) (the “Company”), a global leader in essential water and product quality solutions dedicated to Safeguarding the World's Most Vital Resources™, announced results for the third quarter ended October 2, 2026.
[s3] Key Third Quarter 2026 Results:
[s4] Sales increased 7.5% year-over-year to $1,509 million, with non-GAAP core sales growth of 5.1%
[s5] Operating profit margin was 19.7%, and non-GAAP adjusted operating profit margin was 25.6%
[s6] Net earnings were $253 million, or $1.03 per diluted common share
[s7] Non-GAAP, adjusted net earnings were $290 million, or $1.18 per diluted common share
[s8] Operating cash flow was $323 million and non-GAAP free cash flow was $304 million
[s9] Key Year-to-Date (1) 2026 Capital Allocation and Strategic Actions:
[s10] Deployed $1.1 billion on four strategic acquisitions: In-Situ, GlobalVision, Alfaa UV and Cleanwater1 (2)
[s11] Repurchased $550 million of shares, or 2.4% of outstanding shares (3)
[s12] Early gains from Cost Optimization Program - expected full year 2026 savings now $10-$15 million
[s13] Total sales grew 7.5%, adjusted operating margin expanded 170 basis points and adjusted earnings per share increased 19.2% year over year.
[s14] Core sales grew 5.1%, led by Water Quality at 6.4%, while acquisitions contributed 2.3% to total sales growth,” said Jennifer L. Honeycutt, President and Chief Executive Officer.
[s15] “Year-to-date, we have completed four strategic bolt-on acquisitions and repurchased 2.4% of our outstanding shares, reflecting our disciplined approach to capital allocation and advancing our long-term value creation strategy.”
[s16] “In the fourth quarter, we expect our core sales growth rate to further accelerate to between 5.5% to 6.5% year-over-year.
[s17] Reflecting this growth outlook, early gains from our cost optimization program and our strong third-quarter performance, we raised our full year 2026 adjusted earnings per share guidance to $4.49 to $4.52, representing 15% to 16% growth over the prior year.
[s18] Our rigorous VES-driven execution and strategic investments in 2026 provide a strong foundation for sustained momentum into 2027.
[s19] (1) Year-to-date 2026 capital allocation and strategic actions are as of October 28, 2026
[s20] (2) The acquisition of Cleanwater1 closed on October 5, 2026
[s21] (3) Year-to-date share repurchases as of October 28, 2026.
[s22] 2.4% is calculated off the Company’s outstanding shares as of February 13, 2026
[s23] For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company anticipates non-GAAP core sales growth in the range of 5.5% to 6.5% year-over-year.

# Vulcan Materials Company Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

Vulcan Materials Company reported third-quarter results marked by stronger aggregates pricing, resilient non-aggregates margins, lower overhead costs, and continued shareholder returns.

**Aggregates Performance**
- Segment gross profit came to **$593 million**, or **$9.46 per ton**, while cash gross profit reached **$750 million**, or **$11.95 per ton**.
- Shipments slipped **3%** from the prior year.
- Freight-adjusted selling prices climbed **5%** on a mix-adjusted basis, with the reported increase at **$0.82 per ton**.
- Freight-adjusted unit cash cost of sales rose **7%**, or **$0.72 per ton**, from the prior year.

**Non-Aggregates Performance**
- Non-aggregates segment gross profit was **$72 million**, and cash gross profit was **$88 million**.
- Asphalt gross profit margin stayed strong at **17%**, despite lower shipments and higher liquid asphalt costs.
- Concrete gross profit margin expanded to **9%**.

**Costs and Profitability**
- SAG expense fell to **$137 million**, down **6%** from the prior year.
- SAG expense represented **6.3%** of total revenues in the quarter.

**Cash Flow and Capital Returns**
- Capital expenditures for maintenance and growth projects totaled **$174 million**.
- The company returned **$417 million** to shareholders, including **$350 million** of common stock repurchases and **$67 million** of dividends.
- The ratio of total debt to trailing-twelve months Adjusted EBITDA was **2.0 times**.
- Return on average invested capital on a trailing-twelve months basis was **15.9%**.

**Outlook**
- The company expects to deliver approximately **$2.4 billion** in Adjusted EBITDA for the full year and targets another year of earnings growth in the following year.

**Bottom Line**
The quarter combined firmer pricing and disciplined costs with solid segment margins, shareholder returns, and a maintained full-year earnings outlook.
